reviews.workflow: Delete Selection removes picked brush vertices, edge endpoints or face vertices as one checked convex-hull transaction. NRC Delete/Backspace/Z delete objects only when component mode has no picks, ignoring and preserving exact patch point picks in mixed selections. Patch-only picks never fall back to objects. TB requires component picks and gives its shared Delete command clip-point priority without map history. Background preparation supports cancellation and refuses stale map, selection, tool and profile state. Invalid hulls and protected geometry refuse the whole batch; object deletion removes empty non-world owners. Existing CLI authoring uses the same core services.
reviews.limitation: Native physical input, assistive technology, macOS/Linux and large real-project acceptance remain open. Known 200% expanded-RTL shell crowding remains. Studio refuses all invalid component results atomically, while NRC can retain an invalid brush and alter another. Individual patch points require row/column operations. During NRC clipping the shared geometry Delete command is disabled; existing viewport Delete/Backspace still remove clip points. TB face-derived clip-strategy equivalence and independent-face geometry manipulation remain open. Removed component picks are transient and are not restored by map undo.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate Selection…** previews a rotation by any angle about one axis, around the selection centre, world origin or typed pivot, with texture lock and Valve 220 policy, as one undo step. In component mode it opens **Transform Components…**. `map rotate --axis --degrees --pivot` and `map transform-components --operation rotate` share the services.
reviews.limitation: One axis per rotation; there is no combined X/Y/Z entry, and the modal dialog closes after Rotate rather than staying open for repeated Apply. No palette entry or NRC Shift+R binding. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add X/Y/Z angle fields applied as one Euler XYZ rotation, an Apply button that keeps the dialog open against the refreshed selection, a palette entry and an NRC Shift+R binding.

reviews.workflow: **Resize Selection…** fits objects to typed width, depth and height, keeping the lower corner, centre or upper corner fixed, with Texture Scale Lock; `map resize --size` or `--mins/--maxs` does the same. In component mode, **Transform Components…** and `map transform-components --operation scale --factors` scale picks by factors.
reviews.limitation: Object scaling takes target sizes, not factors, and only positive sizes, so it cannot mirror; the modal dialog closes after one apply. No palette entry or NRC Ctrl+Shift+S binding, which other contexts use for Save As. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a factor mode to the resize service and dialog (X/Y/Z factors about the selection centre or pivot, negative factors as mirrors with winding repair), `map resize --factors x,y,z`, a palette entry and an NRC Ctrl+Shift+S binding that avoids the Save As clash.

reviews.workflow: No automatic caulking yet. Mappers apply common/caulk by hand with **Paint Map Materials**, the surface tools or `map paint-material`. The Region writer and Compile Region already seal and compile part of a map, and generated Quake III levels caulk their own hidden faces. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Hidden faces must be found and caulked by hand. The studio has no compiler profile for VibeMap3's -autocaulk mode and does not read its .caulk output. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add **Auto Caulk Selected** for Quake III. Write the selection, a sealing box and a player start with the region writer. Run VibeMap3 -autocaulk -fulldetail through the compiler wrapper with logs and cancellation. Parse the .caulk face list and apply caulk, liquid caulk or nodraw as one undoable paint edit. Add `map autocaulk`, F4 in the NRC profile and a compiler workflow test.

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, set **Sides** to 3, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**: one undo step in the current material. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 3 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+3 opens Models mode, and the NRC profile binds nothing for this. The triangle's corners are stretched to the box with a corner on the first axis, where NRC's triangle has a face on that axis and overhangs the box. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: On top of the Make Prism… in-place replacement and NRC fit (nrc:BrushPrism), add Make 3- to 9-Sided Prism commands with palette ids and map-view context. Bind them in the NRC profile to keys that do not clash with Ctrl+digit mode switching, or scope Ctrl+3–9 to focused map views.

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, set **Sides** to 4, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 4 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI. The **Box** shape gives an axis-aligned block.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+4 opens Textures mode. A four-sided cylinder puts a corner on each axis, so it makes a diamond inside the box where NRC makes a square on the larger extent. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Cover four sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command: NRC orientation (a face on the first axis), circumscribed sizing, in-place replacement and an NRC profile binding that avoids the Ctrl+digit mode clash.

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, set **Sides** to 5, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 5 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+5 opens Audio mode. Corners are stretched to the box with a corner on the first axis, so the pentagon is turned half a side and scaled differently from NRC's circumscribed one. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Cover five sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command (NRC fit and orientation, in-place replacement, palette id, NRC profile key without the Ctrl+digit clash).

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, set **Sides** to 6, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 6 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+6 opens Packages mode. Corners are stretched to the box with a corner on the first axis, so the hexagon is turned half a side from NRC's, whose circumscribed hexagon overhangs the box. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Cover six sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command (NRC fit and orientation, in-place replacement, palette id, NRC profile key without the Ctrl+digit clash).

Remaining work: Cover seven sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command (NRC fit and orientation, in-place replacement, palette id, NRC profile key without the Ctrl+digit clash).

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, keep **Sides** at 8 (the default), leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 8 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+8 opens Materials mode. VibeStudio's octagon puts corners, not faces, on the axes, so it is turned 22.5 degrees from NRC's, and oblong boxes are fitted rather than circumscribed. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Cover eight sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command (NRC fit and orientation, in-place replacement, palette id, NRC profile key without the Ctrl+digit clash).

reviews.workflow: Choose **Cylinder** on the **Shapes** tab, set **Sides** to 9, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-shape --shape cylinder --sides 9 --axis x|y|z --object brush:ID --texture NAME` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No one-step command or key: Ctrl+9 opens Build mode. Corners are stretched to the box with a corner on the first axis, so the shape is turned half a side and scaled differently from NRC's circumscribed prism. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one shape. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Cover nine sides with the shared Make N-Sided Prism command (NRC fit and orientation, in-place replacement, palette id, NRC profile key without the Ctrl+digit clash).

reviews.workflow: On the **Shapes** tab choose **Cone**, set **Sides**, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. The cone fills the selected world brushes' combined bounds in the current material, as one undo step. **Add Brush…** and `map add-brush` make a new cone; `map add-shape --shape cone --object brush:N` replaces brushes from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: Sides stop at 64, against NRC's 1022. The base corners are stretched to the box with a corner on the first axis, so the cone is turned half a side and sized differently from NRC's circumscribed base. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one cone. No palette command or prompt. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Use the same Make Prism… pattern for a Make Cone… palette command: in-place replacement that keeps brush-entity ownership, the NRC fit option, and a higher side limit.

reviews.workflow: There is no icosahedron or geodesic generator. The nearest route is the latitude-longitude **Sphere** shape on the **Shapes** tab or `map add-shape --shape sphere`. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: No geodesic or truncated-icosahedron construction exists. With the current 128-face bound, 20 or 80 faces (0–1 subdivisions) and the 32-face truncated form fit, but NRC's 320-face second subdivision does not. Remaining work: Add an icosahedron shape (0–1 subdivisions plus a truncate option) built from the geodesic point cloud through addLevelMapBrushHulls. Give it a Shapes tile, Replace Selected Brushes support and `map add-shape --shape icosahedron`, with smoke tests.

reviews.workflow: On the **Shapes** tab choose **Cylinder**, set **Sides**, leave **Axis** on **Across the View** (it follows the active 2D view) and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. One shape fills the selected world brushes' combined bounds in the current material, as one undo step. **Add Brush…** and `map add-brush` create a new prism; `map add-shape --shape cylinder --object brush:N` replaces brushes from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: Sides stop at 64, against NRC's 1022. VibeStudio stretches the corners to the box with a corner on the first axis, so its prisms are turned half a side and sized differently from NRC's, whose faces are tangent to a circle on the larger extent. Brushes of brush entities are refused, and several brushes become one shape instead of converting only the last-selected brush. No palette command or prompt. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Make Prism… palette command that asks for the side count and replaces each selected brush in place, keeping brush-entity ownership. Give radial primitives an NRC fit option (circumscribed circle on the larger extent, face on the first axis) and raise the side limit as far as the component editor allows.

reviews.workflow: There is no rock generator. The nearest route is the **Sphere** shape on the **Shapes** tab, followed by vertex editing or clipping by hand. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Neither the GUI nor the CLI can build a randomised convex brush. An implementation must stay within the 128-face and 256-vertex brush bounds (NRC allows 1000 planes) and should take a seed, since NRC's unseeded rand() output cannot be reproduced for the CLI or tests. Remaining work: Add a rock shape: intersect a seeded set of random planes tangent to the box's inscribed sphere or ellipsoid and insert the resulting corners through addLevelMapBrushHulls. Give it a Shapes tile, Replace Selected Brushes support and `map add-shape --shape rock --sides N --seed S`, with smoke tests.

reviews.workflow: On the **Shapes** tab choose **Sphere**, set **Sides** and **Bands**, choose the pole **Axis** (or **Across the View**) and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. The sphere fills the selection's combined bounds in the current material, as one undo step. **Add Brush…** and `map add-brush --sides --bands` make a new sphere; `map add-shape --shape sphere --object brush:N` replaces brushes.
reviews.limitation: At most 128 faces (sides × bands), where NRC allows up to 31 × 31 planes. VibeStudio fits an ellipsoid to the box; NRC builds a true sphere on the largest extent with its poles on Z. Brush-entity brushes are refused, and several brushes become one sphere. No palette command or prompt. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Make Sphere… palette command that replaces brushes in place, keeps brush-entity ownership and offers an NRC fit (true sphere on the largest extent). Raise the face limit if the component editor bound allows.

reviews.workflow: The **Build** page runs fixed pipelines for each game (BSP, VIS, light), chosen in its **Pipeline** list; compiler paths are set on the **Toolchain** tab. `build plan` and `build run` accept --disable-stage and --stage-args stage=arguments for one run, and `compiler set-path` overrides executables.
reviews.limitation: Users cannot create, rename or save their own pipelines or stage arguments in the GUI. Stage switches and arguments exist only for a single CLI run and in prepared workspaces. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add user-defined pipelines stored in the project manifest, each with a stage list, per-stage arguments and enabled flags. Edit them in a Build page dialog, and have build list, plan and run read them.

reviews.workflow: **Run Build Pipeline** (F7) runs the pipeline chosen on the Build page, which follows the open map's game, and offers to save unsaved map edits to a new file first. **Build and Launch** (F5) also starts the game. `compiler rerun` replays a saved command manifest, and `build run` runs a pipeline again.
reviews.limitation: The chosen pipeline is not remembered across sessions, and F7 does not replay a single compiler-profile run. F5 means Build and Launch rather than a plain rerun, and the NRC profile does not rebind it. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Record the last executed pipeline or compiler profile for each project, and add a build.runLast command bound to F5 in the Radiant profiles.

reviews.workflow: **CSG Intersect** replaces the selected brushes with the one brush where they all overlap. Each face keeps the texture of the face it came from, and the change is one undo step. Brushes that do not overlap, or that belong to different entities, are refused with nothing changed. `map intersect` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: All selected brushes must belong to one entity, whereas NRC accepts brushes from several and keeps the last brush's node. On an empty result NRC deletes the brushes, while VibeStudio refuses safely. The NRC profile lacks Ctrl+Shift+U, which is the global Read Aloud key. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Carve** cuts the selected brushes out of every visible brush they overlap. Opened faces take the carving faces' textures, brushes wholly inside are removed, emptied brush entities go, and the carving brushes stay selected. It is one undo step. The NRC profile binds Shift+U, and `map carve` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: Brushes written on shared source lines are left whole, with a reason given. The fragment layout has not been compared face for face with NRC's split order. Native physical input, macOS/Linux and large real-project acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The Tools tab **Brush** section and the Geometry menu offer **Hollow…** (overlapping walls), **Hollow Touching…** (walls that meet without overlapping) and **Make Room** (walls outside). Each is one undo step, and the first two ask for a thickness. `map hollow --mode overlap|touch|room` and `map extrude-faces` cover them from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: There is no single tool window. Missing: diagonal-joint and extrude-faces hollows, face policies (exclude, or use only, picked faces; by projection or camera), caulk and keep-inner toggles, and whole-brush Shrink and Expand. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build a CSG Tool panel in the Brush section with thickness, face-policy, caulk and keep-inner options. Add Diagonal and Extrude hollow modes and an all-faces offset (Shrink/Expand) in core, and expose them as `map hollow` options.

reviews.workflow: **Make Room** builds walls one grid step thick around the outside of each selected brush, then removes the brush so its volume becomes the room. It is one undo step. `map hollow --mode room --thickness N` does the same from the CLI with any thickness.
reviews.limitation: Walls keep the source textures instead of caulking their hidden faces, and picked faces cannot be left open as doorways. VibeStudio extends the walls to fill the outer corners, where NRC leaves them open. There is no palette registry entry. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add room options to caulk the non-room faces with the game's caulk shader and to leave picked faces open. Share them between the GUI and `map hollow` flags, and register a palette entry.

reviews.workflow: Drive: Look down in **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys), or `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.pitchDown=KEY`, binds downward pitch. It is unbound in **NetRadiant Custom Style**, as upstream; the GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5 and Q3Radiant presets use Z. camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 22.5-degree steps.
reviews.limitation: Discrete pitch stops at -85 degrees and held pitch at -89, not NRC's -90. A bound key needs camera focus, so it does not work from plan views, and it is continuous unless discrete steps are on. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route bound pitch keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, matching NRC's global scope. Consider a -90-degree discrete limit for NRC-family profiles (currently -85), with clamp tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete steps.

reviews.workflow: Drive: Look up in **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys), or `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.pitchUp=KEY`, binds pitch. It is unbound in **NetRadiant Custom Style**, as upstream; the GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5 and Q3Radiant presets use A. camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 22.5-degree steps.
reviews.limitation: Discrete pitch stops at 85 degrees and held pitch at 89, not NRC's 90. A bound key needs camera focus, so it does not work from plan views, and it is continuous unless discrete steps are on. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route bound pitch keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, matching NRC's global scope. Consider a 90-degree discrete limit for NRC-family profiles (currently 85), with clamp tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete steps.

reviews.workflow: The **NetRadiant Custom Style** profile binds Down to Drive: Back, and a plain Down in a plan view also drives the camera backward. **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) or `editor gestures` rebinds it, and camera.discreteDriveKeys switches to 32-unit ground-plane steps. `editor controls` lists the binding.
reviews.limitation: Held drive along the view direction (NRC's non-discrete mode) is the profile default, whereas NRC defaults to discrete ground-plane steps. Plan arrows use grid-based steps unless plan.fixedCameraSteps is on. Camera drive keys need camera focus. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Drive: Down and Fly: Down are available in **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) and are unbound in **NetRadiant Custom Style**, as upstream. Bind one there or with `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.down=KEY`. It moves along world Z; camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 32-unit steps. GtkRadiant-family profiles bind C.
reviews.limitation: A bound key works only while the camera has focus, not from plan views as NRC's accelerator does. It is continuous unless discrete drive steps are enabled. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route bound vertical drive keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, matching NRC's global scope, with overlap warnings and tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete drive steps.

reviews.workflow: **View** > **Camera** > **Focus Camera on Selection** (also **Tools** > **Navigate** and command search) keeps the camera's heading and pitch and moves only the 3D camera onto the line through the selection box's centre. It backs off until all eight corners fit the view's side planes for the current field of view and aspect, never nearer than 64 units; the 2D views stay put, unlike **Frame Selection**. With nothing selected it reuses the last selection of this map load (NRC's work zone), limited to objects the open group allows; hidden objects never count. In the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles, tapping <kbd>Tab</kbd> during mouse look does the same focus. The orbiting view frames the box about its centre. `map camera-focus --object ...` reports the same position.
reviews.limitation: No default key: NRC's window-wide Tab is not reproduced because it would take keyboard focus navigation away. Tab only focuses during mouse look, and users can bind any other key. The fallback re-measures the last selection's objects, rather than keeping NRC's stored work-zone box, after edits. The fit adds an 8-unit near clearance. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the **NetRadiant Custom Style** profile, Up is the camera's Drive: Forward key, and a plain Up in a plan view also drives the camera. **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) or `editor gestures` rebinds it. **Drive keys step 32 units / 22.5 degrees** (camera.discreteDriveKeys) gives NRC's fixed ground-plane steps. `editor controls` prints the binding.
reviews.limitation: The profile defaults to held, continuous drive along the view direction, which matches NRC's non-discrete mode; NRC itself defaults to discrete 32-unit ground-plane steps. Plan arrows step max(grid, 16) units unless plan.fixedCameraSteps is on. Camera drive keys need camera focus. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles, hold <kbd>Tab</kbd> during mouse look. Every turn, fly step or pan lands the 3D camera back on the line through the selection's centre along its view, at the frustum-fit distance. Each wheel notch scales that distance by 2^(-1/8), so eight notches halve or double it, within ±48 notches. The 2D views stay put. Releasing the key, leaving mouse look, losing focus or hiding the camera ends it, and outside mouse look Tab still moves keyboard focus. The key is `camera.focusHoldKey`, set on **Customize Gestures…** > **Camera Keys**, through `editor gestures` or in gesture files; any perspective profile can opt in. `map camera-focus --offset N` reports the same positions.
reviews.limitation: The wheel offset is geometric and never passes through the box centre, unlike NRC's piecewise offset. The box is measured once when the key goes down. Held-button mouse look in other profiles is detected from the pointer's buttons. Native physical-input, screen-reader and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the NetRadiant Custom profile, holding S during mouse look (turned on with a right click) flies the camera backward. Down arrow drives it back both in and out of mouse look. Both can be rebound in **Customize Editor Gestures** or with `editor gestures`, and `editor controls` lists them.
reviews.limitation: Speed scales with the map's size, without NRC's acceleration preference. Semantic Qt tests cover key routing. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Down as Drive: Back, alongside S as Fly: Back. It stays active during mouse look, so holding Down moves the camera backwards continuously along the view direction. Shift and Alt change the speed. Rebind it under **Customize Editor Gestures** > **Camera Keys** or with editor gestures.
reviews.limitation: Speed follows scene size, not NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Down is a Drive binding, so it also flies along the pitched view outside mouse look, where NRC's CameraBack stays level; there is no separate look-only alternative slot. No test asserts the NRC arrow values. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile leaves Fly: Down unbound, as NRC does. Assign a key under **Customize Editor Gestures** > **Camera Keys** (Fly: Down) or with editor gestures netradiant-custom --set camera.flyKeys.down=<key>. During mouse look, holding it lowers the camera along world Z.
reviews.limitation: Movement keys must be single unmodified keys, and Tab, Escape, lock and modifier keys are reserved. Speed differs from NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the NetRadiant Custom profile, a right click turns mouse look on. Holding W then flies the camera forward; outside mouse look W does nothing. Up arrow drives forward in and out of mouse look, as CameraFreeMoveForward2 does. Keys can be rebound in **Customize Editor Gestures** or with `editor gestures`, and `editor controls` lists them.
reviews.limitation: Speed scales with the map's size, not NRC's speed and acceleration preferences. Semantic Qt tests cover key routing. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Up as Drive: Forward, alongside W as Fly: Forward. Drive keys stay active during mouse look, so holding Up flies forward continuously along the pitched view direction, as NRC's free-move arrow does. Shift and Alt change the speed. Rebind it under **Customize Editor Gestures** > **Camera Keys** or with editor gestures.
reviews.limitation: Speed follows scene size, not NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Up is a Drive binding, so it also flies along the pitched view outside mouse look, where NRC's CameraForward stays level; there is no separate look-only alternative slot. No test asserts the NRC arrow values. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the NetRadiant Custom profile, holding A strafes the camera left both during mouse look (fly keys) and outside it (drive keys), as NRC's CameraFreeMoveLeft and CameraStrafeLeft do. During mouse look, Left arrow also strafes, matching CameraFreeMoveLeft2. Keys can be rebound in **Customize Editor Gestures** or with `editor gestures`.
reviews.limitation: Speed scales with the map's size, without NRC's acceleration preference. Semantic Qt tests cover key routing. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Left as Drive: Turn left. **Turn keys strafe during mouse look** is on by default, so Left turns when idle and strafes left during mouse look, matching NRC's modal arrows. The key and the setting can be changed under **Customize Editor Gestures** or with editor gestures.
reviews.limitation: The strafe-in-look assertion runs against the GtkRadiant profile, which shares the default; NRC has no test of its own. Speed differs from NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the NetRadiant Custom profile a right click starts mouse look, and holding D then strafes right (Fly: Right, active only during mouse look). D is also Drive: Right, so it strafes right outside mouse look too, as NRC's CameraStrafeRight does. Shift speeds flight up and Alt slows it. Rebind it under **Customize Editor Gestures** > **Camera Keys** or with editor gestures.
reviews.limitation: Speed follows scene size with Shift/Alt multipliers, not NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration time. Shared key-motion tests cover modal fly/drive routing, but the NRC W/A/S/D values have no dedicated assertion. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Right as Drive: Turn right. With **Turn keys strafe during mouse look** on by default, Right turns when idle and strafes right during mouse look. The key and the setting can be changed under **Customize Editor Gestures** or with editor gestures.
reviews.limitation: The strafe-in-look assertion runs against the GtkRadiant profile, which shares the default; NRC has no test of its own. Speed differs from NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Like NRC, the NetRadiant Custom profile leaves Fly: Up unbound. Assign a key under **Customize Editor Gestures** > **Camera Keys** (Fly: Up) or with editor gestures netradiant-custom --set camera.flyKeys.up=<key>. During mouse look, holding it raises the camera along world Z, never sideways because of pitch.
reviews.limitation: Movement keys must be single unmodified keys, and Tab, Escape, lock and modifier keys are reserved; NRC's shortcut system has no such limits. Speed differs from NRC's CamMoveSpeed and acceleration. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In **NetRadiant Custom Style**, Left is Drive: Turn left in the camera, and a plain Left in a plan view turns the camera. During mouse look the turn keys strafe, as NRC's free move does. **Customize Editor Gestures** or `editor gestures` rebinds it. camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 22.5-degree steps.
reviews.limitation: The profile turns continuously by default (NRC's non-discrete mode); NRC defaults to 22.5-degree steps. Plan arrows turn 15 degrees per press unless plan.fixedCameraSteps is on. Camera drive keys need camera focus. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **3D Wireframe** (map.preview-wireframe) switches between wireframe and shaded drawing. The **Textures** box above the views, also on the **View** tab, switches between flat shading and package textures. Between them they reach three of NRC's four modes.
reviews.limitation: There is no next-mode command and no Shift+] binding. The Levels camera has no textured-plus-wireframe mode, **Textures** has no command id or palette entry, and turning **3D Wireframe** off returns to flat shading even with **Textures** ticked. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Next Camera Mode command that cycles Wireframe, Flat, Textured and Textured with edges (ModelViewport::setShowEdges already exists). Give Textures in Camera a command id, save the chosen mode, announce it in the status bar, and bind Shift+] in the NRC profile.

reviews.workflow: **3D Wireframe** (map.preview-wireframe) and the **Textures** box above the views, also on the **View** tab, choose wireframe, flat-shaded or textured drawing directly. There is no step order to go back through.
reviews.limitation: There is no previous-mode command and no Shift+[ binding. The Levels camera has no textured-plus-wireframe mode, **Textures** has no palette entry, and leaving wireframe always returns to flat shading. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build this with Next Camera Mode as a Previous Camera Mode command over the same four-mode cycle, with a palette entry, a status message and the Shift+[ binding in the NRC profile.

reviews.workflow: In **NetRadiant Custom Style**, Right is Drive: Turn right in the camera, and a plain Right in a plan view turns the camera. The turn keys strafe during mouse look. Rebind it in **Customize Editor Gestures** or with `editor gestures`. camera.discreteDriveKeys gives fixed 22.5-degree steps.
reviews.limitation: Continuous turning (NRC's non-discrete mode) is the profile default, and plan arrows turn 15 degrees unless plan.fixedCameraSteps is on. NRC defaults to 22.5-degree steps. Camera drive keys need camera focus. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Holding the profile's slow flight modifier (Alt by default) cuts the map-scaled flying speed to 0.3. **Customize Editor Gestures** or `editor gestures` changes which modifier does this.
reviews.limitation: There is no persistent lower speed, no decrease command, no keypad binding and no readout. The slow modifier works only while it is held. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build this with Increase Camera Speed as a Decrease Camera Speed command over the same saved setting, clamped to a minimum, with a palette entry, a status readout and Shift+Keypad - in the NRC profile.

reviews.workflow: Flying speed scales with the size of the map. Holding the profile's fast modifier (Shift by default) triples it, and holding the slow modifier (Alt) cuts it to 0.3. Both modifiers are set in **Customize Editor Gestures** or with `editor gestures`.
reviews.limitation: There is no stepped speed that persists, no increase command, no NRC keypad binding and no speed readout. A modifier changes the speed only while it is held. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a saved camera speed setting used by ModelViewport::flySpeed, with an Increase Camera Speed command and palette entry. Show the speed in the status bar, expose a field through `editor gestures`, and bind Shift+Keypad + in the NRC profile.

reviews.workflow: **NetRadiant Custom Style** binds A to Drive: Left while the camera has focus, and to Fly: Left during mouse look. Rebind it in **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) or with `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.left=KEY`. camera.discreteDriveKeys switches to 32-unit ground-plane steps.
reviews.limitation: The key strafes only while the camera has focus; plan views do not route it as NRC's global accelerator does. The default is continuous held motion rather than NRC's discrete steps. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route the bound camera strafe keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, with overlap warnings and plan-focus tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete drive steps.

reviews.workflow: **NetRadiant Custom Style** binds D to Drive: Right while the camera has focus; during mouse look, D is Fly: Right. **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) or `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.right=KEY` rebinds it. camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 32-unit ground-plane steps.
reviews.limitation: Strafing works only while the camera has focus; plan views do not route D as NRC's global accelerator does, so a 2D-focused user must click the camera first. The default is held, continuous motion rather than NRC's discrete steps. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route the bound camera strafe keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, reporting overlaps through levelCameraShortcutWarnings, with plan-focus tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete drive steps.

reviews.workflow: Drive: Up and Fly: Up exist in **Customize Editor Gestures** (Camera Keys) and are unbound in **NetRadiant Custom Style**, as upstream. Bind one there or with `editor gestures --set camera.driveKeys.up=KEY`. Motion follows world Z, and camera.discreteDriveKeys gives 32-unit steps. GtkRadiant-family profiles bind D.
reviews.limitation: A bound key works only while the camera has focus, not from plan views as NRC's accelerator does. It moves continuously unless discrete drive steps are enabled. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route bound vertical drive keys from plan views when no plan command claims them, matching NRC's global accelerator scope, with overlap warnings and tests. Optionally default the NRC profile to discrete drive steps.

reviews.workflow: **Cap Patch…** previews and adds planar radial caps on chosen boundaries of one source patch (first and last rows by default), in the source or a chosen material, with planar or boundary UVs, an optional centre and Invert, as one undo step. Closed ends become discs and open arcs close along their chord. Shift+C opens it in the GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5 and Q3Radiant profiles. `map cap-patch` does the same.
reviews.limitation: Cylinder and Endcap ends close as discs and half-discs, but NRC's Bevel (quarter sector to the arc's centre), Inverted Bevel and Inverted Endcap fills cannot be made, because an open arc always closes on its chord. Each run caps one patch, not every selected patch in the current texture, and the NetRadiant Custom profile does not bind Shift+C. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add NRC cap styles as seam patches built from each first and last row with NRC's width checks: Bevel (sector to the corner opposite the arc's middle control), Inverted Bevel and Inverted Endcap, plus matching Endcap and Cylinder topology. Apply them to every selected patch in the current material, expose them in the dialog and `map cap-patch --style`, and bind Shift+C in the NetRadiant Custom profile.

reviews.workflow: **View** > **Camera** > **Level Camera** (<kbd>End</kbd> in the NetRadiant Custom, NetRadiant, GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5/1.6, Q3Radiant and DoomEdit profiles; also **Tools** > **Navigate** and command search) keeps the 3D camera where it stands, sets pitch to zero and turns the heading to the nearest 22.5 degrees. The 2D views, the map and its undo history are unchanged, and the status bar announces the new heading. In the orbiting VibeStudio Default view it levels the orbit. `map camera-focus --level --camera-yaw Y --camera-pitch P` reports the same angles.
reviews.limitation: Exact half steps round away from zero instead of Radiant's +11 bias. QeRadiant and DarkRadiant leave End unbound until their sources confirm it. Native physical-input, screen-reader and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Centre Views on Selection** moves every 2D view to the selection's centre without changing zoom. **Centre Plan Views on Camera** covers the empty-selection case by centring the plans on the camera position or orbit target, also without changing zoom. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Shift+Tab to **Centre Views on Selection**.
reviews.limitation: The camera fallback is a separate command without a key (Centre Views on Selection is disabled with nothing selected). No CLI route. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Not covered. **Help > About VibeStudio** (and `about show`) report the running version, and releases are published on GitHub as described in the release documentation. Existing control: None.
reviews.limitation: There is no update link and no update check. Any automatic version comparison would need opt-in consent under the offline and AI-free rules; a plain link would not. Remaining work: Add a help.checkForUpdates command that opens the latest-release page for the repository named in the release metadata. Compare VERSION with the latest tag only after the user opts in.

reviews.workflow: There is no camera draw-distance control. The Levels camera projects with an unbounded far plane. The nearest substitutes are **Region** and **Filters** on the **View** tab: they hide objects by box or by kind, not by distance from the camera. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: There is no far-clip distance, no step command and no status readout. Region works on a box and also changes the plan views. Once this is built, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance will still be open. Remaining work: Give the Levels camera a saved cubic-clip distance: a bounded far plane that OpenGL, Vulkan and picking all respect. Add Shorter Draw Distance commands with palette entries, NetRadiant Custom (NRC) Ctrl+[ binding and a status readout. Build it alongside Toggle Cubic Clip.

reviews.workflow: There is no camera draw-distance control. The Levels camera already draws everything in front of it, with no far limit. **Region** and **Filters** on the **View** tab control what is shown by box or by kind, not by distance. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: There is no adjustable far-clip distance, step command or readout to extend. Once this is built, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance will still be open. Remaining work: Build this with Shorter Draw Distance as a Longer Draw Distance command over the same saved cubic-clip distance. Clamp it to a bounded range, add a palette entry and the NRC Ctrl+] binding, and show the distance in the status bar.

reviews.workflow: There is no floor-stepping command. Fly the camera down with a vertical fly key assigned in **Customize Editor Gestures** (the NetRadiant Custom profile binds none by default), or use **Go to Coordinates…** with **Take the camera there too** ticked. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Nothing finds standing heights from the scene. docs/EDITOR_PROFILES.md records floor stepping as unsupported in the GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5, NetRadiant and Q3Radiant profiles. Page Down already runs Lower Floor on selected Doom sectors, so an NRC binding needs profile scoping. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build this with Camera Floor Up. Search the same visible and selected bounds for the nearest standing height below the camera, falling back to the lowest underside. On Doom maps, use sector floors plus eye height. Bind PgDn only in the NRC profile.

reviews.workflow: Levels **Textures** tiles are painted onto a transparent pixmap, so decoded alpha (including fence index 255) lets the panel colour show through. The **Textures** page preview has a **Transparency** checkbox that draws a checkerboard behind the image. The **Materials** workbench has **Engine View** > **Checkerboard Behind**, and `material render --no-checker` turns the checker off.
reviews.limitation: Levels tiles have no checkerboard and no opaque mode, so transparent texels blend into the theme background and cannot be switched. The checkerboard toggles exist only in single-image previews and are not remembered. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a remembered Transparency toggle to the Levels Textures tab header. When on, draw the shared checker tile behind tiles; when off, flatten alpha. Include the setting in the thumbnail cache key.

reviews.workflow: Select the entities (or brushes of brush entities), picking last the one whose colour to use, and choose Normalise Entity Colour (Edit > Keys, the entity right-click menu, the Tools tab, the palette; no default key, as upstream). Its _color is divided by its brightest channel (black becomes 1 1 1) and written as fractions to every target's _color, each keeping its trailing brightness, as one undo step. The result is remembered as the next picker colour. The command is disabled when the last-picked entity has no _color, and refused with a reason when it does not parse. `map entity-colour --normalise` does the same, and `--normalise --each` normalises every entity's own colour, skipping ones without a colour.
reviews.limitation: Like Set Entity Colour, worldspawn is reached only when selected itself and hidden entities are skipped. Normalise Each is a CLI-only VibeStudio extension with no GUI command. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Select lights or other entities, or brushes of a brush entity, and choose Set Entity Colour… (K in the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles; Edit > Keys, the entity right-click menu, the Tools tab, the palette). A colour dialog opens on the _color of the entity picked last, or on the colour chosen last (levels/entityColour). The choice is written to the _color key of every selected entity and of every entity holding a selected brush or patch, in each key's own 0-1 or 0-255 form with its trailing brightness, as one undo step. Nothing to colour, a locked target or one outside the open group is reported before the picker opens. `map entity-colour --colour "r g b"|#rrggbb` (with --object or --where, optional --key) does the same and saves to a new path. The Inspector's colour swatch picker and `map edit` remain for single keys.
reviews.limitation: Deliberate differences from NRC: worldspawn is coloured only when selected itself, not through a selected world brush (NRC's walker also writes worldspawn), and existing 0-255 keys stay 0-255 where NRC always writes %g fractions. Hidden entities are skipped and counted rather than written. The GtkRadiant 1.6 profile has no K binding because it was not verified against a checkout. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Move Primitives to First Entity (unbound by default, as in NRC; Brush Entity menu, Tools > Entities, palette) uses the entity of the first-selected item as the target, with the same key-keeping, emptied-entity removal and one-step undo. `map move-to-entity --target first` matches it.
reviews.limitation: Same as Move Primitives to Entity: definition-free point-entity detection, locked/linked refusal and synchronous execution. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Select brushes and patches, then an item of the entity that should receive them, and choose Move Primitives to Entity (Ctrl+M in the NetRadiant Custom profile; Brush Entity menu, Tools > Entities, view bar Create menu, palette). The entity owning the last-selected item, worldspawn included, takes the other selected primitives and the visible ones of other selected brush entities, keeping its keys. Emptied source entities are removed, all as one undo step; ids, groups and visibility are kept. `map move-to-entity --target last` (default) or `--target entity:N` does the same.
reviews.limitation: Point entities are recognised without definitions (an origin and no primitives) and refused as targets. Locked or linked content is refused instead of propagated. Runs synchronously rather than as a cancellable placement task. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the **Map** sidebar tab, the **Entity Definitions** section has a path field. Pressing **Load**, or Enter in the field, re-reads the named .def, .fgd or .ent file or folder, or the project's usual definition folders when the field is empty, with the built-in catalogue standing in if none are found. It then refreshes the Create classes, the Inspector and the Health checks without reloading the map. `entity definitions` and `entity validate` read the files on every run.
reviews.limitation: Load is a button with no palette command or shortcut, and no file watcher notices edits to loaded definition files. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Move to World** resolves each selected brush, patch or brush entity to its owner. It moves all of the owner's brushes and patches to worldspawn and removes the entity and its keys, as one undoable step through the guarded scene-edit service. It is in the Brush Entity context menu, the Tools tab **Entities** group and the **Create** tools. `map move-to-world` (alias `ungroup-entity`) does the same from the CLI. Its shared registry entry lets editor profiles and **Keyboard Shortcuts** give it a key; no profile does by default.
reviews.limitation: It works on Quake-family .map files only, and refuses brushes that share source lines with other map text. Only the core function is tested; no UI or CLI test triggers it. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Move Selected to World (Brush Entity menu, Tools > Entities, palette; unbound as in NRC) moves only the selected brushes and patches, plus the visible ones of selected brush entities, to worldspawn as one undo step. Entities keep their other primitives and keys, and go once empty. A moved brush joins its old entity's scene node, otherwise the open group or current layer. `map move-to-world --selected-only` does the same.
reviews.limitation: Hidden primitives of a selected entity stay in it. Locked or linked content is refused. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **File > Quit** (Ctrl+Q) closes the window through the same close handler as the title bar. It first stops or waits for running package, model and audio work, then asks about unsaved code tabs, unsaved map edits and staged package changes before quitting.
reviews.limitation: No test quits with an unsaved map: tests cover app.quit's registry entry, a saved map closing without a prompt and code-tab Cancel. Native physical-input acceptance and the macOS application-menu Quit and Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Expand Selection to Whole Entities** replaces each selected brush or patch of a brush entity with that entity, which carries all its primitives, and leaves world primitives and point entities as they are. It is in the Levels **Tools** tab Select group.
reviews.limitation: Selected world brushes stay as they are instead of expanding to every visible world primitive. No palette entry or CLI query; the NRC profile lists Shift+E **Expand Selection** as an unimplemented binding. It sets the selection directly, without the shared selection worker's hidden, locked and closed-group checks. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Register a palette entry and wire the NRC profile's Shift+E binding; add an NRC policy that expands selected world primitives to all visible world brushes and patches; run it through the shared object-selection worker for visibility, lock and group checks; add a read-only `map select-*` query.

reviews.workflow: Select an object in each layer and choose **Expand Selection to Layers** (**Select** menu above the views, **Edit** > **Layers**, the right-click menu, the **Tools** tab or command search; <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Q</kbd> in the NetRadiant Custom profile). Every visible, unlocked, unfiltered object in those layers joins the selection, nested groups included. Closed groups stay whole and are left out when a member is hidden, locked or filtered; an open group keeps the result inside it. It runs on the cancellable worker and adds a selection undo step only in the TrenchBroom profile. `editor scene select --objects … --expand-layers` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio layers hold nested groups, not NRC's nested layers, so a layer's groups stand in for NRC's child layers. Ctrl+Q stays Quit, so the NetRadiant Custom profile uses Ctrl+Shift+Q. Brush entities join through their brushes. Doom lines and vertices belong to a layer only when assigned to it. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Select Siblings** comes closest: a selected brush entity becomes its children, and a child brush selects its owner's other selectable primitives, honouring hidden, locked, filtered and closed-group objects. `map select-siblings` runs the same read-only query.
reviews.limitation: Siblings follow TrenchBroom's hierarchy: a world brush or point entity selects every object in its layer, including entities and other owners' children, instead of world primitives only. There is no Ctrl+E binding in the NRC profile. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add **Expand Selection to Primitives** on the shared object-selection worker: replace brush-entity wrappers with their visible children and add each selected primitive's owner primitives (world primitives only for world brushes), with NRC Ctrl+E and a `map select-*` query mode.

reviews.workflow: No areaportal kind in the **Filters** section. Workarounds: **Select All of Type** on the areaportal material then **Hide Selection**, which does not persist as a filter, or unticking **Brush Entities**, which hides Quake II func_areaportal along with every door and trigger. Existing control: None; the Filters section has no Areaportals check box.
reviews.limitation: No filter kind, command, Alt+3 binding or CLI. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an areaportals kind matching brushes with any areaportal-textured face or the CONTENTS_AREAPORTAL (0x8000) content bit, plus Quake II func_areaportal entities; translate its title, register a checkable command and add core tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Clip** filter names brushes whose every face texture contains 'clip' or carries clip contents, so botclip brushes hide along with player and weapon clip. To hide bot clip alone, use **Select by Texture…** with common/botclip, or query `texture:botclip` in the **Objects** filter and press Enter, then use **Hide Selection**. `map find` and `map visibility` cover the same steps from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: There is no separate bot clip kind, donotenter is not matched, and the selection workaround is temporary and one-off. There is no shortcut (NRC binds Alt+M) or CLI filter report, and classification is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Split a 'botclip' filter kind (botclip and donotenter, all faces) out of Clip for Quake III maps. Give it a check box, a bindable toggle (NRC profile Alt+M) and tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Caulk** check box in the **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab hides brushes whose every face uses a texture named caulk, in the 2D views and camera with a count; the choice persists. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Caulk check box (levelFilter-caulk).
reviews.limitation: Caulk faces on otherwise textured brushes stay drawn, and Quake's skip counts as **Hint and Skip** rather than caulk. The NetRadiant Custom profile lists a Toggle Caulk Filter entry (editor.filters.toggle-caulk) with no key or wired command; no palette entry, Alt+6 binding, CLI or automated test. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add per-face hiding of caulk faces in the plan and camera renderers, treat Quake's skip as caulk for Quake 1 maps, wire the NRC profile's editor.filters.toggle-caulk entry to a checkable command bound to Alt+6, and add core and rendering tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Clip** check box in the **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab hides brushes whose every face uses a texture named with clip, or carries Quake II player or monster clip bits, in the 2D views and camera with a count; the choice persists. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Clip check box (levelFilter-clip).
reviews.limitation: Quake III shaders with surfaceparm playerclip under other names, and clip-shaded patches, are missed; bot clip is folded in rather than separate. No command, palette entry, Alt+7 binding or CLI; no automated test covers the kind. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Match surfaceparm playerclip through the material library, include clip-shaded patches, split bot clip into its own kind, register a checkable command bindable to Alt+7 and add core tests.

reviews.workflow: No clusterportal kind in the **Filters** section. Selecting the material with **Select All of Type** and using **Hide Selection** is the only workaround and does not persist as a filter. Existing control: None; the Filters section has no Clusterportals check box.
reviews.limitation: No filter kind, command, Alt+9 binding or CLI. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Quake III clusterportals kind for brushes whose every face uses common/clusterportal or carries CONTENTS_CLUSTERPORTAL (0x100000); register a checkable command and add core tests.

reviews.workflow: There is no Decals filter kind. As a workaround, query `texture:decals/` in the **Objects** filter, press Enter to select the matches and use **Hide Selection**. `map find` lists the same brushes, and `map visibility --mode hide` previews the hide.
reviews.limitation: The workaround hides a snapshot temporarily. New decal brushes stay visible, **Show All Hidden** clears it, the query matches decals/ anywhere in a texture path, and there is no toggle, saved state or shortcut (NRC binds Shift+D). Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a 'decals' filter kind for Quake III maps: brushes with any face under decals/. Give it a View tab check box, a bindable toggle (NRC profile Shift+D) and classification tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Detail** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides brushes with the detail content flag, plus the brushes and patches of func_detail* entities. It applies in the 2D views and the camera, shows a live count and is remembered between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Detail check box (levelFilter-detail)
reviews.limitation: A brush counts as detail if any face carries the detail flag, whereas NRC requires all faces. There is no command id, palette entry, profile shortcut (NRC binds Ctrl+D) or CLI, and classification has no dedicated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Toggle Entities with the View tab check box, View > Filters > Entities, Select > Filters on the view bar, command search, or Alt+2 in the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles. It hides every entity that is not worldspawn, func_group or func_detail* (point entities, plus brush entities such as doors and triggers with their brushes), the inverse of World Brushes as in NRC. It applies to all views and is saved. `map filters` reports it.
reviews.limitation: Show > Entities separately controls whether point-entity markers are drawn in the 2D views. Already-selected objects stay selected. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Toggle Func Groups with the View tab check box, View > Filters > Func Groups, Select > Filters on the view bar, or command search. It hides entities whose class is exactly func_group, with their brushes and patches, in every view, and the state is saved. Give it a key in Controls if wanted; NRC has no default key either. The Scene tab's own groups keep their separate visibility. `map filters` reports the kind.
reviews.limitation: No default key, as in NRC. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Hint and Skip** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides brushes with any face whose texture name contains hint, any face named skip, or any face carrying the Quake II/III hint or skip surface flags. It shows a live count and is remembered between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Hint and Skip check box (levelFilter-hint)
reviews.limitation: Matching relies on texture names and face flags, not shader definitions. It is broader than NRC: skip faces count, including Quake's skip, which NRC files under Caulk. There is no command id, palette entry, profile shortcut (NRC binds Ctrl+H) or CLI, and classification is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: There is no Lightgrid filter kind. As a workaround, use **Select by Texture…** with common/lightgrid, or type `texture:lightgrid` in the **Objects** filter and press Enter, then use **Hide Selection**. `map find` lists the same brushes, and `map visibility --mode hide` previews the hide without writing the map.
reviews.limitation: The workaround hides a snapshot temporarily. Lightgrid brushes added later stay visible, both selection routes take a brush with any lightgrid face rather than all faces, and **Show All Hidden** clears it. There is no one-step toggle or saved filter state. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a 'lightgrid' filter kind for Quake III maps: brushes whose every face uses a common/lightgrid texture. Give it a View tab check box, a bindable toggle command and classification tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Lights** check box in the **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab hides entities whose class begins with light in the 2D views and camera, with a count; the choice persists between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Lights check box (levelFilter-lights).
reviews.limitation: The prefix rule also hides light_* classes such as Quake's light_flame variants, which NRC's exact match keeps. No command, palette entry, Alt+0 binding or CLI; no automated test covers the kind. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Liquids** check box in the **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab hides brushes with any face named with *, water, slime, lava or a liquid folder, or carrying Quake II liquid content bits, in the 2D views and camera with a count; the choice persists. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Liquids check box (levelFilter-liquids).
reviews.limitation: Quake III shaders declaring surfaceparm water, lava or slime under other names are missed, and the name rule can catch solid textures such as a lavarock wall. No command, palette entry, Alt+5 binding or CLI; no automated test covers the kind. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Resolve Quake III face shaders through the material library and match surfaceparm water/lava/slime ahead of the name heuristic; register a checkable command bindable to Alt+5; add core tests over Quake, Quake II and Quake III fixtures.

reviews.workflow: The **Models** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides entities whose class begins with misc_model or misc_gamemodel. It applies in the 2D views and the camera, shows a live count and is remembered between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Models check box (levelFilter-models)
reviews.limitation: Detection uses fixed class prefixes rather than entity definitions. It misses model_static, other misc_*model classes and definition-declared model classes, and catches any class that merely begins with misc_model. There is no command id, palette entry, profile shortcut (NRC binds Shift+M) or CLI, and classification is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: There is no way to hide them. The Levels **Textures** tab draws a framed placeholder for a name with no picture, and its tooltip and accessible text say it is not in the open package. The Health texture check counts missing textures, and `map textures` reports them. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Tiles with missing images always stay in the list, including in the Map and Package listing. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open once built. Remaining work: Add a remembered Hide Image Missing header toggle to the Levels Textures tab that hides tiles with no resolved package or editor image. Leave a note giving the hidden count so the texture check still reports them.

reviews.workflow: On Quake III maps, the **Patches** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides every patch in the 2D views and the camera. It shows a live count. VibeStudio remembers the state, and **Show Every Kind** brings everything back. The map, builds and packages are unchanged. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Patches check box (levelFilter-patches)
reviews.limitation: The filter is a check box only. It has no command id, palette entry, profile shortcut (NRC binds Ctrl+P) or CLI report, and the manual's Filters list omits it. Viewport masking is tested, but filter classification has no dedicated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Paths** check box in the **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab hides entities whose class begins with path_ in the 2D views and camera, with a count; the choice persists between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Paths check box (levelFilter-paths).
reviews.limitation: Same class rule as NRC, but there is no command, palette entry, Alt+8 binding or CLI, and no automated test covers the kind. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Toggle Point Entities with the View tab check box, View > Filters > Point Entities, Select > Filters on the view bar, or command search. It hides point entities other than lights and misc_model/misc_gamemodel, which keep their own Lights and Models filters, as NRC's filter_entity_point does. An entity counts as a brush entity, never a point entity, when it owns brushes or patches or when the built-in catalogues define its class as a brush class, so an empty door stays under Brush Entities. The state is saved, and `map filters` reports the kind.
reviews.limitation: Point and brush classes come from the built-in Quake, Quake II and Quake III catalogues, not from a project's loaded .def/.fgd/.ent definitions. No default key, as in NRC. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Sky** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides brushes with any face that matches one of these rules: the texture name starts with sky, it lies under skies/, it is skyportal, or the face carries the sky surface flag. It shows a live count and is remembered between sessions. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Sky check box (levelFilter-sky)
reviews.limitation: Detection uses texture names and face flags, not skyparms in shader scripts, so Quake III sky shaders with other names are missed and unrelated textures named sky* are caught. There is no command id, palette entry, shortcut or CLI, and classification is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Resolve Quake III sky faces through parsed shader skyparms from the material library, keep the name and flag rules for Quake and Quake II, and add a bindable toggle command and classification tests.

reviews.workflow: VibeStudio has no structural filter. The View tab's **World Brushes** filter hides all worldspawn geometry, detail brushes included, and **Detail** does the opposite job. The Objects query cannot test content flags, so structural brushes cannot be selected and hidden that way either. **Make Structural** and **Make Detail** change the flags but do not filter anything. Existing control: None. The closest controls are Levels > View tab > Filters > World Brushes and Detail.
reviews.limitation: Structural brushes cannot be hidden on their own, and no query or selection command names them. No toggle command, shortcut (NRC binds Ctrl+Shift+D) or CLI exists. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a 'structural' filter kind: on Quake II/III maps, brushes without the detail content flag outside func_detail; on Quake maps, worldspawn and brush entities other than func_detail*. Give it a View tab check box, a bindable toggle (NRC profile Ctrl+Shift+D) and classification tests on Quake, Quake II and Quake III fixtures.

reviews.workflow: No translucent kind in the **Filters** section. The Materials module already classifies materials as translucent (Quake II SURF_TRANS33/66, Doom 3 coverage) and parses Quake III qer_trans and surfaceparms, but the level filters do not consult it. Existing control: None; the Filters section has no Translucent check box.
reviews.limitation: No filter kind, command, Alt+4 binding or CLI. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a translucent kind: Quake II faces with SURF_TRANS33/SURF_TRANS66 (0x10/0x20) and Quake III shaders with qer_trans, alphaFunc or fog resolved through the material library, for brushes and patches; refresh when materials reload; add core tests.

reviews.workflow: The **Triggers** check box in the View tab's **Filters** section hides entities whose class begins with trigger_, together with their brushes. It applies in the 2D views and the camera, shows a live count and is remembered between sessions. **Show Every Kind** restores all filters. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Triggers check box (levelFilter-triggers)
reviews.limitation: The class rule matches NRC. However, there is no command id, palette entry, profile shortcut (NRC binds Ctrl+Shift+T) or CLI report, and classification has no dedicated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: No route, as no supported game uses visportal brushes. Quake II and Quake III areaportals are reviewed under nrc:FilterAreaportals.
reviews.limitation: Visportals are an idTech4 (Doom 3) mechanism and NRC registers the toggle only for doom3. VibeStudio's level editor targets Doom WADs and Quake, Quake II and Quake III .map files (LevelMapFormat); brushDef3 faces parse only as a Quake III dialect, with no Doom 3 game target, and idTech1-3 compilers have no visportals. Out of scope while the level editor targets idTech1-3; it would need an idTech4 game target first.

reviews.workflow: Toggle World Brushes with the View tab check box, View > Filters > World Brushes, the view bar's Select > Filters menu, command search, or Alt+1 in the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles. It hides worldspawn's brushes and patches together with func_group and func_detail* entities and everything they own, as NRC's filter_entity_world does. It applies to every plan view and the camera, filtered objects cannot be picked, and the state is saved between sessions. `map filters` reports the kind's count and objects.
reviews.limitation: Already-selected objects stay selected when the kind is hidden. The GtkRadiant profiles carry no Alt+1. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Find Brush by Number…** pre-fills from the last selected object and also reads a pasted compiler line such as 'Entity 0, Brush 12'. It then selects and frames the object, or the entity itself. Brushes and patches are counted together, as compilers count them. `map find --number entity[,brush]` reports the same object.
reviews.limitation: The found object replaces the selection; NRC adds it. The views zoom to it rather than only recentring. `map find --number` has no dedicated CLI test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Find and Replace Textures…** opens a modeless window. Picks on the Textures tab, on the Textures surface or from **Reveal Material** fill the field that last had focus, which the window states in words. While the window is open, activating a tile fills that field instead of applying the texture. **Search in** chooses **Whole map**, **Selected objects** or **Picked faces** (Select Textured, Find or camera picks, plus query-picked whole patches). A live summary counts matches, changes and skipped uses. **Find** adds the matching faces and patches through the Select Textured service, within the selection when that scope is chosen; Doom maps select lines and sectors. **Replace** is one undo step, skips hidden, filtered, locked and out-of-context uses, and leaves the window open. CLI: `map replace-texture` (`--object`, or `--face` with optional `--context`; JSON reports `scope`, `targets` and `skipped`), `map select-textured --within-selection` and `map textures`.
reviews.limitation: NRC's single Apply button, which searches when Replace is empty, is split into Find and Replace buttons; Enter still finds while Replace is empty. Find leaves closed groups out until they are opened, as Select Textured does, while Replace includes them. The CLI's `--face` scope takes brush faces only; whole patches use `--object`. Native physical input, screen readers and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Fit Texture 1 × 1** (the **Fit 1 × 1** button on the **Surfaces** tab) fits one repeat to each targeted face and whole patch as one undo step. **Surface Alignment…** fits any U and V repeat counts with a live preview, and `map align-textures --fit U,V` does the same for faces and patches from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: The quick button is fixed at one repeat; other counts need the modal dialog, which takes brush faces only, or the CLI. Patches keep their relative coordinate spacing instead of being re-tiled as an even grid. The NetRadiant Custom profile lists Ctrl+F as a reserved Fit Texture binding that routes to no command, so Ctrl+F stays on Find. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Fit V** on the **Surfaces** tab fits one repeat down V for faces and whole patches and leaves U untouched. **Surface Alignment…** with Fit and U repeats set to 0, or `map align-textures --fit 0,N`, fits any V count the same way.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio's **Fit Texture Height** command (the **Fit V** button) keeps U unchanged, which is NRC's Height Only behaviour despite the name; there is no proportional height fit, so matching the aspect needs a manual U scale afterwards. The button is fixed at one repeat and has no command-catalogue entry. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Share the keep-proportions Fit option proposed for FitTextureWidth: scale U by the V fit factor and align it to its minimum, expose a proportional Fit Height command in the command catalogue and Surfaces tab, add the CLI flag, and test faces of each dialect.

reviews.workflow: **Fit Texture Height** (the **Fit V** button on the **Surfaces** tab) fits one repeat down V and keeps U, for the Selection or **Picked Faces** and whole patches, as one undo step. **Surface Alignment…** with Fit and U repeats 0, or `map align-textures --fit 0,N`, fits any V count.
reviews.limitation: The quick button is fixed at one repeat; other counts need the modal dialog (brush faces only) or the CLI. Patches keep their U coordinates, whereas NRC re-tiles them to one U repeat. The command has no profile key, matching NRC's lack of a default key, and only core service tests cover its effect. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Fit U** on the **Surfaces** tab fits one repeat across U for faces and whole patches and leaves V untouched. **Surface Alignment…** with Fit and V repeats set to 0, or `map align-textures --fit N,0`, fits any U count the same way.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio's **Fit Texture Width** command (the **Fit U** button) keeps V unchanged, which is NRC's Width Only behaviour despite the name; there is no proportional width fit, so matching the aspect needs a manual V scale afterwards. The button is fixed at one repeat and has no command-catalogue entry. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a keep-proportions option to LevelSurfaceOperation::Fit that scales the zero axis by the fitted axis's factor and aligns it to its minimum. Expose proportional Fit Width and Fit Height commands in the command catalogue and Surfaces tab, add a matching CLI flag to `map align-textures`, and test faces of each dialect.

reviews.workflow: **Fit Texture Width** (the **Fit U** button on the **Surfaces** tab) fits one repeat across U and keeps V, for the Selection or **Picked Faces** and whole patches, as one undo step. **Surface Alignment…** with Fit and V repeats 0, or `map align-textures --fit N,0`, fits any U count.
reviews.limitation: The quick button is fixed at one repeat; other counts need the modal dialog (brush faces only) or the CLI. Patches keep their V coordinates, whereas NRC re-tiles them to one V repeat. The command has no profile key, matching NRC's lack of a default key, and only core service tests cover its effect. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The Levels **Textures** tab always draws uniform square tiles. Its **Tile Size** header menu offers Small, Medium, Large or Largest and remembers the choice. Images keep their aspect ratio and small ones are enlarged with crisp pixels. Once the level preview has decoded a texture, its tooltip gives the source width and height. Existing control: Levels Textures tab Tile Size header button (levelTextureTileSize)
reviews.limitation: Only the fixed mode exists. There is no sizing relative to native dimensions, no minimum-size clamp and no command id for the tile choices. Package-only tiles do not state their size. Tile Size has no automated test. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Native Size choice to Tile Size that sizes each tile from its source dimensions times a scale, clamped to minimum and maximum sizes. This needs non-uniform layout and thumbnails cached per size. Register commands for the choices and add a UI test.

reviews.workflow: Not covered. **Maximize or Restore Active View** and **Reset Layout** give the views more room inside the window, and the operating system can maximise the window. Existing control: None.
reviews.limitation: No full-screen command exists. macOS full-screen spaces and Linux window-manager behaviour would need their own acceptance. Remaining work: Add a checkable view.fullScreen command that toggles Qt::WindowFullScreen and is saved with the window state. Bind it to F11 in the Radiant profiles and cover it with a shell test.

reviews.workflow: **Smaller Grid** halves the shared Levels grid, and now goes below 1 unit to 0.5, 0.25 and 0.125. Run it from the palette or press [. NetRadiant Custom, GtkRadiant and TrenchBroom profiles keep that Levels default; TrenchBroom also binds -. Both grid lists follow and the matching **Grid** command is checked. Every pane, snapped drag, nudge, drawn brush, clip point and the 3D camera's move grid use the new size. The status bar reports it and it is kept for the next session. In the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles each step also turns **Snap** on, as GridPrev does; the gesture preference editing.gridChangeEnablesSnap turns that off. Binary Doom and Hexen maps store whole units, so there it stops at 1 unit and the status bar says why.
