reviews.limitation: The command is disabled at the finest size: 0.125, or 1 on binary Doom and Hexen maps. So [ there does not turn **Snap** on, whereas NRC's GridPrev is always enabled. Fine lines are drawn only when they are at least 6 pixels apart; otherwise they thin out and the status lines give the drawn spacing. The CLI keeps no working grid; scripted edits pass --grid, fractions included, to each command. Acceptance with physical keys and on macOS and Linux is still open.

reviews.workflow: **Larger Grid** doubles the shared Levels grid, now up to 1024 units. Run it from the palette or press ], the Levels default that the NetRadiant Custom, GtkRadiant and TrenchBroom profiles keep (TrenchBroom also binds + and =). The view-bar grid list and the sidebar **View** tab's **Grid** list follow, every pane updates and the status bar reports the size, which is kept for the next session. In the NetRadiant Custom and NetRadiant profiles each step also turns **Snap** on, as GridNext does, and the status bar says so; a gesture preference (editing.gridChangeEnablesSnap) turns that off per profile.
reviews.limitation: At 1024 the command is disabled, so ] there no longer turns **Snap** on, whereas NRC's GridNext stays enabled and still sets snapping. The CLI keeps no working grid; editor controls --json reports gridSizes and gridChangeTurnsSnapOn, and scripted edits pass --grid. Acceptance with physical keys and on macOS and Linux is still open.

reviews.workflow: `map paste --from other.map` inserts a map file's objects as one texture-locked edit, at original coordinates, at an offset, at the camera or along a ray. In the GUI, map text on the clipboard goes in with **Paste at Original Position**. **Insert Prefab…** places saved .vprefab assemblies with remapped target links.
reviews.limitation: No GUI command picks a .map file to merge; the text must go through the clipboard. Paste accepts at most 8 MiB / 4,194,304 characters and 8,192 blocks, so large maps cannot be imported whole. Pasted target names are not renamed, and .bsp files need a separate VibeMap3 convert run. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an **Import Map…** File command and palette entry. It should read a .map on a worker, preview object counts, rename clashing target names and insert through the existing paste service at original coordinates as one undo step. Lift the paste limits for file input with a streamed path, offer .bsp conversion through the VibeMap3 convert profile, and add a UI test.

reviews.workflow: **Invert Patch Facing** turns every selected patch round as one undo step, with UVs kept on their points. It is in the Tools tab's **Patches** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor as **Invert Facing**. `map patch-matrix --op invert` or `map edit-patch --invert` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+I; a UI test presses it on a patch and checks the exact undo.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio mirrors each row's columns, whereas NRC reverses the rows. Facing matches, but later first/last row or column commands reach different edges. Tests only check that inverting twice restores a patch; the facing flip itself, the matrix operation and the CLI routes are untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip U** in the Levels **Surfaces** tab (also **Flip Texture U** under Edit > Surface Adjustments) mirrors U on the selected patches and brush faces when the target is **Selection**. The shared surface worker applies the batch as one undo step. `map align-textures --flip u --object patch:ID` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio mirrors about the patch's UV centre, while NRC negates coordinates about zero, so the result can land at a different offset. The command also changes selected brush faces, and the **Picked Faces** target skips patches. The NetRadiant Custom profile has no key for it, because Ctrl+Shift+I runs **Initialize Project Manifest** window-wide. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip V** in the Levels **Surfaces** tab (also **Flip Texture V** under Edit > Surface Adjustments) mirrors V on the selected patches and brush faces when the target is **Selection**, as one undo step. `map align-textures --flip v --object patch:ID` scripts it. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Shift+I.
reviews.limitation: The mirror pivots on the patch's UV centre rather than zero, so the result can land at a different offset. The command also changes selected brush faces, and **Picked Faces** skips patches. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Choose View > Filters > Invert Filters, Select > Filters > Invert Filters on the view bar, the Invert Filters button in the Filters section of the Levels View tab, or Invert Filters in command search. Every kind the open map's format offers flips in the saved filters list: hidden kinds come back and shown kinds hide. Kinds saved for other formats stay. Filters reapply to every plan view and the camera, and the status bar says how many kinds are now hidden. The map, selection and undo are unchanged. Show Every Kind (map.reset-filters) is Radiant's Reset filters. `map filters <map> --off ... --invert` previews the result.
reviews.limitation: Inverting covers only the kinds VibeStudio filters, so Radiant's areaportal, translucent, clusterportal, structural, lightgrid, botclip and decal flags have no counterpart. No default key, as in NRC. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Choose **Move to Layer…** (<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Q</kbd> in the NetRadiant Custom profile) for a menu of the layers at the pointer, or the **Move to Layer** submenu of the right-click menu, as in TrenchBroom. Picking a layer moves the selection into it as one undo step. A member of a closed group moves its whole group; a brush of a brush entity moves the entity. Entries are greyed out with the reason when there is no selection, the selection is already in that layer, or the layer or the objects are locked. Objects moved into a hidden layer leave the selection. `editor scene move-to-layer --id <layer UUID|default> --objects … --output …` does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: The menu lists Default and the named layers only; groups are not offered (use Assign selection in the Outliner). Moving is refused while a group is open. The popup has no New Layer entry and no layer colours. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Make Detail** (Levels Geometry tools, Tools tab **Brush** group) sets the detail content flag on every face in Quake II and III maps. In Quake maps it moves the brushes into a `func_detail` for VibeMap2. Either way it is one undo step with an activity record. `map detail --object brush:N --output` uses the same service. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Alt+D.
reviews.limitation: When every selected brush is already detail the command is refused with a message, where NRC reapplies silently; brushes whose face lines cannot be rewritten in place are skipped. The core service is tested, but the GUI and CLI routes have no dedicated tests. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Make Structural** (Levels Geometry tools, Tools tab **Brush** group) clears the detail flag on every face in Quake II and III maps. In Quake maps it returns `func_detail` brushes to worldspawn. Either way it is one undo step with an activity record. `map detail --structural --object brush:N --output` uses the same service. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Alt+S.
reviews.limitation: When every selected brush is already structural the command is refused with a message, where NRC reapplies silently; brushes whose face lines cannot be rewritten in place are skipped. The core service is tested, but the GUI and CLI routes have no dedicated tests. Native input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Statistics** section on the Levels sidebar's **Map** page lists counts for entities, target links, brushes (solved and degenerate), faces, patches, Doom objects and textures. It also shows the format, engine, bounds and issue counts. `map inspect` prints the same statistics, with --json for automation.
reviews.limitation: No count of entities by class and no group or in-game entity counts. No command, palette entry or M shortcut opens the section. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a sortable class and count table, plus group and in-game entity counts, to levelMapStatistics, the Statistics section and `map inspect --json`. Add a **Map Info** command that opens the Statistics section, with M in the NRC profile, a palette entry and a UI test.

reviews.workflow: **Transpose Patch** swaps rows and columns of every selected patch, turning its facing as Radiant does, as one undo step; transposing twice restores the patch. It is in the Tools tab's **Patches** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op transpose` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Shift+M.
reviews.limitation: The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Maximize or Restore Active View** (map.maximizeView) enlarges the level pane focused last and cancels any unfinished drag; repeating it restores the previous pane sizes. It is bound to F12 in the NRC profile and Shift+Z in Hammer and J.A.C.K. **Equalize View Sizes** evens the panes out.
reviews.limitation: The target is the pane focused last rather than the pane under the cursor. The CLI offers only persistent layouts (`editor layout`), not this temporary state. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Horizontal** mirrors along X in the top and front views and along Y in the side view, the same mapping as upstream. It mirrors about the bounds centre as one undo step, with Texture Lock and Repeat recording for objects, and also handles picked components and Doom geometry. `map flip --axis` gives exact axes.
reviews.limitation: NRC snaps the pivot to the grid, so its flip can shift the selection by a grid step; VibeStudio mirrors in place. Component-mode flips use component UV Lock and do not feed Repeat. Neither NRC nor VibeStudio's NRC profile binds a default key. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Vertical** mirrors along Y in the top view and along Z in the front and side views, the same mapping as upstream. It mirrors about the bounds centre as one undo step, with Texture Lock and Repeat recording for objects, and also handles picked components and Doom geometry. `map flip --axis` gives exact axes.
reviews.limitation: NRC's grid-snapped pivot can shift the result by a grid step; VibeStudio mirrors in place. Component-mode flips do not feed Repeat. Automated UI coverage of Flip Vertical uses Doom maps, and core tests cover Quake axes. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip X** (Edit > Transform, the Transform menu, the Tools tab or the palette) mirrors the selection along the world X axis whatever view is active, as one undo step, with Texture Lock and Repeat recording. In component mode it mirrors the picked components under component UV Lock. With a top or front view active, **Flip Horizontal** does the same. `map flip --axis x` writes a save-as copy.
reviews.limitation: Flips mirror about the exact bounds centre in every profile. NRC's grid-snapped flip pivot is deliberately not copied: it moves odd-width selections, and TB avoids it with a half-grid pivot. For on-grid selections the result matches TB's. Component-mode flips do not feed Repeat. No profile binds Flip X, as in NRC. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Y** mirrors the selection along the world Y axis whatever view is active, as one undo step, with Texture Lock and Repeat recording, and mirrors picked components in component mode. **Flip Vertical** in the top view, or **Flip Horizontal** in the side view, does the same. `map flip --axis y` writes a save-as copy.
reviews.limitation: Flips mirror about the exact bounds centre in every profile rather than NRC's grid-snapped pivot; this is deliberate, and matches TB's result for on-grid selections. Component-mode flips do not feed Repeat. Unbound in every profile, as in NRC. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Z** mirrors the selection along the world Z axis whatever view is active, as one undo step, with Texture Lock and Repeat recording, and mirrors picked components in component mode. It is disabled for Doom-format maps. **Flip Vertical** in the front or side view does the same; the UI test drives it on a Quake brush as well as Doom. `map flip --axis z` writes a save-as copy.
reviews.limitation: Flips mirror about the exact bounds centre in every profile rather than NRC's grid-snapped pivot; this is deliberate. Component-mode flips do not feed Repeat. Doom geometry does not flip along Z. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Extrude Faces** pushes or pulls picked brush faces along their normals, **Split Extrusion** creates a separate brush, and **Extrude Faces Precisely…** takes an exact distance. **Duplicate with Offset…** builds linear arrays, and **Repeat Last Commands** replays a recorded clone and transform on a new selection. `map extrude-faces`, `map duplicate` and `map repeat` automate them.
reviews.limitation: There is no single Build mode and no chain-building gesture: extrusion is a component-mode tool, and clones come from separate commands. Upstream's own behaviour is a placeholder at the pinned revision, so parity is judged against its stated intent. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: If NRC finishes the tool, add a Build entry to the Levels tool bar. A face drag would go to the shared extrusion service and a modified drag would build an offset clone chain recorded for Repeat. Until then, keep the existing commands.

reviews.workflow: The Levels **Select** tool is the default and behaves like the QE4 drag. A drag on the selection moves it, a drag beside it resizes the sides facing the pointer (the `resize-selection` gesture), and an empty 2D drag draws a brush. In the camera, a drag moves the selection across the ground, or vertically with Alt. **Edit Faces** moves single brush planes. **Customize Editor Gestures** and `editor gestures` adjust these per profile.
reviews.limitation: Resizing remaps the selection's box instead of translating the brush planes that face the pointer, so oblique brushes stretch rather than moving their sloped faces. The Select tool has no Alt plane or vertex drags and no Ctrl+Alt extrude gesture, and camera brush creation needs **Draw Brush**. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Offer an NRC-style plane-drag resize that translates the brush planes facing the press point. Add the Alt plane/vertex and Ctrl+Alt extrude modifiers to the Select tool's gesture table, routed through the existing face-extrusion and component services.

reviews.workflow: **Shear Tool** is a checkable command. Turning it on gives the 2D views shear handles; turning it off, or pressing Escape, returns to the default **Select** drag behaviour. One key assigned in **Keyboard Shortcuts** therefore alternates between the two. `map shear` covers automation.
reviews.limitation: The shear handles cover only part of NRC's Transform tool: there is no box scaling, rotation or pivot. They work only in 2D views, and the NetRadiant Custom profile does not bind Q to the toggle. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Bind the Shear Tool, or a future combined Transform tool, to Q in the NetRadiant Custom profile. Make the command return to the Select tool explicitly and keep the tool bar's check state in step.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate 90° Left** and **Right** turn the selection in the active view. **Rotate Selection…** previews any angle about the selection centre, the world origin or a custom pivot, with Texture Lock. In component mode, **Rotate Components** gives XYZ rotation rings about a movable pivot (**Move Component Pivot**). `map rotate` and `map transform-components` automate both.
reviews.limitation: Whole objects cannot be rotated by dragging: interactive rings exist only for picked components. There is no screen-axis ring or trackball rotation, no draggable object pivot, no Rotate tool on the Levels tool bar and no R key in the NetRadiant Custom profile. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an object Rotate tool that reuses the component rotation rings and pivot for whole brushes, patches and entities. It would publish through the numeric rotation service (Texture Lock, Valve 220 policy), add a screen ring with free rotation and Shift angle snapping, and come with a tool-bar entry and an NRC R binding.

reviews.workflow: There is no alternating command. In component mode, **Rotate Components** and **Scale Components** are separate checkable tools, and each can be given a key in **Keyboard Shortcuts**. Whole objects use **Rotate Selection…** and **Resize Selection…**.
reviews.limitation: No single command toggles between rotate and scale, and whole objects have no rotate or scale tool modes to toggle. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Once object Rotate and Scale tools exist, add a bindable map command that alternates between them, falling back to the component tools in component mode. List it in the NRC profile catalogue without a default key.

reviews.workflow: Objects are resized by dragging the box handles in a 2D view or the labelled X/Y/Z face handles in the camera. **Resize Selection…** takes exact sizes and the point that stays fixed, and **Texture Scale Lock** stretches textures with the geometry. In component mode, **Scale Components** gives axis and uniform handles about the shared pivot. `map resize` and `map transform-components` automate both.
reviews.limitation: Interactive object resizing is driven by the bounding box and anchored at the opposite side, not centred on a pivot. Objects have no uniform scale handle, no draggable pivot and no Scale tool mode; only the numeric dialog sets a fixed point. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an object Scale tool that reuses the component axis and uniform scale handles and the pivot. It would publish through resizeLevelMapSelection or the affine transform service, honour Texture Scale Lock, offer Shift for equal axes and Ctrl for grid-snapped sizes, and come with a tool-bar entry and a bindable command.

reviews.workflow: **Shear Tool** adds side handles in every 2D view that slant the selection about the opposite side, snapped to the grid. **Shear…** slants about the centre by an exact angle. Resize handles and dragging cover scaling and moving. In component mode, **Shear Components** offers six shear directions. `map shear` and `map transform-components` automate them.
reviews.limitation: No single box manipulator combines skew, scale, rotation and translation. Object shear handles work only in 2D views, their corners do nothing, and object pivots cannot be dragged. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Extend the Shear Tool into a combined Transform tool: edge skew, side and corner scaling, rotation and free movement on the selection box in plan and camera views. It would share a draggable object pivot with the other manipulators and use the existing affine transform service.

reviews.workflow: The Levels **Select** tool moves objects by dragging: freely in a 2D view, and in the camera across the ground, or vertically with Alt. Arrow-key nudges and **Move Selection…** give exact offsets. In component mode, **Move Components** adds camera XYZ handles and a centre handle. `map move`, `map move-components` and `map transform-components` cover automation.
reviews.limitation: Whole objects have no translate manipulator: no axis arrows, no free-move square and no draggable pivot. Object drags are limited to the view plane or the camera's ground/vertical split. The Levels tool bar has no Translate tool, and the NetRadiant Custom profile binds nothing to W outside mouse look. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an object-level Translate tool to the Levels tool bar. It would extend the camera component move handles (XYZ arrows and centre handle) to whole brushes, patches and entities in plan and camera views, add a draggable shared pivot, publish through the shared move service with Texture Lock, and come with a bindable command and an optional NRC W key outside mouse look.

reviews.workflow: Texture alignment is numeric and stepped. The **Surfaces** tab and **Inspector** shift, rotate, scale, fit, justify and flip faces, picked faces or patches. **Surface Alignment…** previews detailed changes, and **Edit Patch Control Points…** edits patch UVs. Doom walls can be dragged with **Drag Textures in Camera**. `map align-textures`, `map edit` and `map edit-patch` automate these edits.
reviews.limitation: Brushes and patches have no direct on-face UV manipulator: no texture drag, no rotation circle, no U/V scale or skew handles and no pivot. There is no UV tool on the Levels tool bar and no G key in the NetRadiant Custom profile. The production record lists direct UV manipulation as open. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build a camera UV tool. It would project the face or patch texture grid, expose drag, rotate, scale and skew handles about a movable pivot with vertex and edge snapping, and publish each drag as one undo step through the shared surface and texture-transform services.

reviews.workflow: **Nudge Down Along Z** (Radiant-family profiles, NetRadiant Custom included: keypad -) moves the selection, or picked vertices, edges or faces, one grid step down world Z from any focused level view, the camera included, or from the palette. It takes priority over view zoom and is one undo step with Texture Lock (component UV lock for components), scene locks and open-group context. The command is remappable and in Edit > Nudge and the Tools tab. `map nudge --direction z-down` works headlessly for --object or --set.
reviews.limitation: Doom maps refuse Z nudges. Split and extrusion component nudges along Z are refused. Physical keypad input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Nudge Up Along Z** (Radiant-family profiles, NetRadiant Custom included: keypad +) moves the selection, or picked components, one grid step up world Z from any focused level view or the palette. It takes priority over view zoom and is one undo step with Texture Lock (component UV lock for components), scene locks and open-group context. The command is remappable and in Edit > Nudge and the Tools tab. `map nudge --direction z-up` works headlessly.
reviews.limitation: Doom maps refuse Z nudges. Split and extrusion component nudges along Z are refused. Physical keypad input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Move to Camera** (Ctrl+Shift+V in the NetRadiant Custom profile; **Edit** > **Duplicate and Move**, the **Tools** tab and command search) applies Paste to Camera's centre rule to the live selection: the centre of its paste bounds (point entities sized from the loaded definitions) goes to the camera, or the orbit view's focus centre, by a translation snapped to the grid while Snap is on. It is one Move placement through the placement worker, so it is one undo step, is recorded for Repeat, keeps object identities, order and source spans, and leaves the clipboard alone. In a component mode it moves the picked components by the snapped translation from their centre. `map move --camera x,y,z [--grid N]` is the CLI route.
reviews.limitation: Quake-family text maps only; Doom maps are refused. A selection already centred at the current grid size is refused with a message rather than recording an empty step. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Natural** in the Levels **Surfaces** tab (**Natural Texture Mapping** under Edit > Surface Adjustments) runs naturalLevelPatchTexture on the selected patches, and Radiant's natural projection on brush faces. It uses the material size and Quake III's 0.5 default scale, as one undo step. `map align-textures --natural 0.5,0.5 --object patch:ID` scripts it.
reviews.limitation: The command needs the material's dimensions from the open package or `--texture-size`, and it also resets selected brush faces. Ctrl+N opens **New Map** in Levels, so the NetRadiant Custom profile gives Natural no key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **New Map…** opens a dialog to choose the game (Quake, Quake II, Quake III, Doom or Hexen) and an empty map or a room with a player start, then asks about unsaved edits. The untitled map opens in Levels, and **Save** sets its path. Ctrl+N works while Levels has focus. `map new` writes the same document to --output.
reviews.limitation: The dialog asks for a game and starting geometry, where NRC silently uses the current game. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Next Build Problem** (F4) lists a leak first: it opens Levels and frames the whole trail. The Health row and **Frame Leak Trail** in the 2D context menu do the same. **Load Leak Trail…** draws a trail by hand.
reviews.limitation: There is no point-by-point walk. The views frame the whole trail, the camera is not moved to or aimed along each point, and the trail is not drawn in the camera. The NRC profile has no Ctrl+Shift+K for this. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add Next and Previous Leak Point commands that keep a cursor into the loaded trail. Each step centres the 2D views, places the camera on the point aimed at the next one, and announces 'point N of M' and the ends of the trail. Register palette entries and the NRC Ctrl+Shift+K and Ctrl+Shift+L bindings.

reviews.workflow: **Next 2D View** steps Top, Front and Side in the same order; the NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Tab. In three-plan layouts it moves focus to the next pane. **Cycle Map View** also steps through 3D in one-pane layouts.
reviews.limitation: In one-plan layouts the new projection refits the whole map instead of keeping zoom and centring on the selection or camera; in three-plan layouts focus moves instead of recentring. The plan view also owns Ctrl+Tab (add next object), and no test presses Ctrl+Tab under this profile. No CLI route. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: On a projection change keep the current zoom and centre on the selection bounds, or the camera when nothing is selected (at least for Radiant profiles), instead of MapViewport::setProjection's zoomToFit; let the profile's Ctrl+Tab take precedence over the plan view's own Ctrl+Tab, and cover both with a UI smoke test.

reviews.workflow: View labels and HUD text are painted with the interface font, so **Typeface** and **Text scale** in Settings > **Appearance and Language** (or the global --set-font and --set-text-scale CLI options) change them, as do **Larger Text** and **Smaller Text**. The high-contrast theme helps legibility.
reviews.limitation: View labels have no font of their own: family and size follow the whole interface (HUD text at 90% of it), so a different view font cannot be chosen without changing menus too. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux font rendering acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an optional view-label font family and size preference, applied through viewportHudFont and the map view labels, with HUD layout tests at each text scale.

reviews.workflow: **Help > Documentation** opens the bundled HTML manual. It looks beside the executable and in the macOS Resources and Linux share layouts, falls back to the online manual on GitHub, and reports a failed open in the status bar. The command palette lists it by its menu label. Existing control: Help menu > Documentation (command help.documentation, which has no registry id); command palette entry by label.
reviews.limitation: No default key: F1 is unbound (Shift+F1 opens About). The command is not in the semantic shortcut registry and has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux bundle-path acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Open Map…** picks a Quake-family .map or a Doom WAD, asks about unsaved edits, then loads it on a cancellable worker. The shortcut is Ctrl+M by default and Ctrl+O in the GtkRadiant, NetRadiant Custom, TrenchBroom and QuArK profiles. **Recent maps** on the Levels start page reopens files. `map inspect` reads a map from the CLI without editing it.
reviews.limitation: The dialog starts in the project folder (or home), not a game maps folder or the current map's folder, and the unsaved-edits question comes after the file is chosen. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Bevel** on the Levels **Shapes** tab builds the same three-column quarter-round with the same control layout. Draw it, add it at the view centre, or use **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-patch --shape bevel` and `map add-shape --shape patch-bevel` script it.
reviews.limitation: Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. **Add Patch…** lacks this shape, although the manual lists it. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Apply Natural mapping on creation, offer the bevel in the Add Patch… dialog, and add a palette entry.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Cone** on the Levels **Shapes** tab with **Segments** 4, **Add Patch…** (Cone) and `map add-patch --shape cone` each make a nine-column, three-row cone. The cone fits a box along the chosen axis and uses the Textures material.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio's cone tapers straight, with the middle ring at half radius, which matches NRC's Exact Cone rather than this bulging classic profile. To match, drag the middle row in **Edit Patch Control Points…**. Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a classic Radiant cone variant, with a full-radius middle ring, to createLevelPatch, the Shapes tab and `map add-patch`, and apply Natural mapping on creation.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Cylinder** on the Levels **Shapes** tab with **Segments** 4 makes the same nine-column ring, using the Textures material and the view axis. Use **Draw in a View**, **Add at View Centre**, or **Replace Selected Brushes**, which fills their bounds in one undo step. **Add Patch…** offers a nine-column cylinder with adjustable rows. `map add-patch --shape cylinder` defaults to 9x3.
reviews.limitation: New patches get one stretched texture repeat (UV 0 to 1) instead of Natural mapping, and the ring's seam starts on the opposite side from NRC's. The Shapes tab defaults to eight segments (17 columns), **Replace Selected Brushes** takes only world brushes, and **Add Patch…** always stands the cylinder on Z. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Apply Natural mapping from the material's dimensions when a patch shape is created. Default patch shapes to four segments, Radiant's 9x3. Register palette entries for the patch prefabs.

reviews.workflow: No equivalent. Patch control points can only be moved deliberately, through **Edit Patch Control Points…**, **Edit Vertices** in the views, or `map edit-patch` and `map transform-components`. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Nothing randomises patch control points, so roughening a surface means moving many points by hand. Once built, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance would also be open. Remaining work: Add **Deform Patch…**: offset every control point of the selected patches by a random amount up to a maximum along X, Y or Z, with a seed so runs repeat, as one undo step. Add a `map deform-patch` CLI command and core, UI and CLI tests.

reviews.workflow: **Delete First Patch Columns** joins the first two spans of each row through their shared point using the same middle-control formula, two columns fewer, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op delete-first-columns` does the same.
reviews.limitation: A three-column patch refuses the whole selection rather than falling back to deleting rows as NRC does. The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Delete First Patch Rows** joins the first two spans of each column through their shared point, two rows fewer, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op delete-first-rows` does the same.
reviews.limitation: One three-row patch refuses the whole selection, whereas NRC skips it and edits the others; only that refusal is tested, not a successful deletion. The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Delete Last Patch Columns** joins the last two spans of each row into one with the same middle-control rule, as one undo step; after **Add Patch Columns** it restores the original grid exactly. It is in the Tools tab, Geometry and context menus and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op delete-last-columns` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Shift+Keypad −.
reviews.limitation: A three-column patch refuses the whole selection rather than falling back to rows. The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Delete Last Patch Rows** joins the last two spans of each column into one, two rows fewer, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op delete-last-rows` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Keypad −.
reviews.limitation: One three-row patch refuses the whole selection, whereas NRC skips it. The core test checks only the resulting row count, and the CLI route is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Patch End Cap** on the Levels **Shapes** tab builds the same five-column arch with the same control layout. Draw it, add it at the view centre, or use **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-patch --shape endcap` and `map add-shape --shape patch-endcap` script it.
reviews.limitation: Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. **Add Patch…** lacks this shape, although the manual lists it. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Apply Natural mapping on creation, offer the end cap in the Add Patch… dialog, and add a palette entry.

reviews.workflow: **Insert Patch Columns** (Levels **Tools** tab, **Patch Rows and Columns**) splits the first span of each selected patch exactly, as one undo step. The **Rows and Columns** menu in **Edit Patch Control Points…** does the same on the draft. `map patch-matrix --op insert-columns --patch ID` scripts it. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Shift+Keypad +.
reviews.limitation: At 31 columns VibeStudio refuses the edit, where NRC silently inserts rows. `map patch-matrix` has no dedicated CLI test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Insert Patch Rows** splits the first span of each column exactly, adding two rows as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry toolbar and viewport context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op insert-rows` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Keypad +; a UI test presses it and checks two new rows and the exact undo.
reviews.limitation: One patch at the row limit refuses the whole selection, whereas NRC skips that patch and edits the rest. The core test checks only the new grid size of Insert Rows (exact splitting is tested on columns), and the CLI route is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Add Patch Columns** (Levels **Tools** tab, **Patch Rows and Columns**) splits the last span of each selected patch exactly, as one undo step. **Add Columns** in the **Rows and Columns** menu of **Edit Patch Control Points…** works on the draft. `map patch-matrix --op add-columns --patch ID` scripts it.
reviews.limitation: At 31 columns VibeStudio refuses the edit rather than inserting rows. `map patch-matrix` has no dedicated CLI test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Add Patch Rows** splits the last span of each column exactly, adding two rows as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu (**Add Rows**). `map patch-matrix --op add-rows` does the same.
reviews.limitation: The label differs: NRC's Insert Last Rows is VibeStudio's **Add Patch Rows**. One patch at the row limit refuses the whole selection, whereas NRC skips that patch. Add Rows itself has no direct test (only Add Columns and Insert Rows are checked), and the CLI route is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Sphere** on the Levels **Shapes** tab with **Segments** 4 and **Bands** 2 builds the same 9x5 control rings. Draw it, add it at the view centre, or replace selected brushes. `map add-patch --shape sphere` defaults to 9x5, and `map add-shape --shape patch-sphere` fits a box.
reviews.limitation: The Shapes tab defaults to 8 segments and 4 bands (17x9), and the seam starts on the opposite side. Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. **Add Patch…** has no sphere. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Default patch spheres to 4 segments and 2 bands, apply Natural mapping on creation, and offer the sphere in the Add Patch… dialog.

reviews.workflow: **Square Patch Cylinder** on the Levels **Shapes** tab builds the same corner-started 9x3 tube along the chosen or view axis, with the Textures material. Draw it, add it at the view centre, or use **Replace Selected Brushes**. `map add-patch --shape square-cylinder` and `map add-shape --shape patch-square-cylinder` script it.
reviews.limitation: Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. **Add Patch…** offers only plane, cylinder and cone, although the manual lists all seven shapes. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Apply Natural mapping at creation, add the missing shapes to the Add Patch… dialog (or correct docs/manual/levels.md), and add palette entries.

reviews.workflow: **Thicken Patch…** takes a thickness (grid step by default), a direction (surface normals or X, Y or Z) and **Close the open edges with walls**. It adds a facing-away copy and walls to each patch's entity as one undo step and selects them; folded edges and closed seams get no walls. It is in the Tools tab and the Geometry and context menus. `map thicken-patch` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+T.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio accepts fractional thickness, whereas NRC uses whole units, and it selects only the new pieces, whereas NRC keeps the source selected too. The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Cone** on the Levels **Shapes** tab builds the same straight tangent-intersection cone: **Segments** 3 to 15 gives 7 to 31 columns. `map add-patch --shape cone --segments N --rows M` sets both dimensions. **Add Patch…** offers a nine-column cone with adjustable rows, and the **Re-disperse** commands follow up.
reviews.limitation: The Shapes tab always makes three rows and **Add Patch…** always makes nine columns standing on Z, so only the CLI sets both dimensions. There is no Square option at creation. Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Rows control and a Square option for round patch shapes in the Shapes tab and the Add Patch… dialog, and apply Natural mapping on creation.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Cylinder** on the Levels **Shapes** tab uses the same tangent-intersection construction: **Segments** 3 to 15 gives 7 to 31 columns. `map add-patch --shape cylinder --segments N --rows M` sets both dimensions. **Re-disperse Patch Columns** and **Re-disperse Patch Rows** (or `map patch-matrix`) space the result afterwards.
reviews.limitation: The Shapes tab always makes three rows and **Add Patch…** always makes nine columns, so only the CLI sets both. There is no Square option at creation. Mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Rows control and a Square (re-disperse) option for round patch shapes in the Shapes tab and the Add Patch… dialog, and apply Natural mapping on creation.

reviews.workflow: **Patch Sphere** on the Levels **Shapes** tab uses the same construction. **Segments** 3 to 15 (7 to 31 columns) and **Bands** 2 to 15 (5 to 31 rows) match NRC's ranges. Draw it, add it at the view centre, or replace selected brushes. `map add-patch --shape sphere --segments N --bands M` scripts it, and the **Re-disperse** commands follow up.
reviews.limitation: There is no Square option at creation, and mapping is one stretched repeat rather than Natural. **Add Patch…** has no sphere, although the manual says it does. There is no palette entry or profile key. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Square (re-disperse) option and Natural mapping on creation, and add the sphere, with segments and bands, to the Add Patch… dialog.

reviews.workflow: **Preferences** (Ctrl+,) opens Settings at **Appearance and Language**, which also holds the editor profile and 3D renderer; Accessibility, AI and Extensions have their own categories. Level options sit in the Levels **View** sidebar, **Clipper Options** and **Customize Editor Gestures**. From the CLI, the global --set-* options, `editor select`, `editor clipper` and `editor gestures` change preferences, and `accessibility report` prints them.
reviews.limitation: NRC's single dialog is spread across several studio surfaces, so some camera, 2D view and brush options live in sidebars or the CLI rather than on one page. NRC's plain P key is not bound in the NRC profile. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Previous Build Problem** (Shift+F4) cycles back through the last build's problems, and the leak entry frames the whole trail in Levels. The Health row and **Frame Leak Trail** in the 2D context menu also frame it.
reviews.limitation: There is no trail cursor to step back along, the camera is not placed or aimed per point, and the trail is not drawn in the camera. The NRC profile has no Ctrl+Shift+L for this. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Implement it together with Next Leak Point: a shared trail cursor, camera and 2D placement per point, start and end announcements, a palette entry, and the NRC Ctrl+Shift+L binding.

reviews.workflow: **Re-disperse Patch Columns** moves each span's middle control halfway between its ends along the rows, leaving UVs alone, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op redisperse-columns` does the same.
reviews.limitation: The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Re-disperse Patch Rows** moves each span's middle control halfway between its ends down the columns, leaving UVs alone, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op redisperse-rows` does the same.
reviews.limitation: Only the column variant has a direct core test; the row variant and the CLI route are untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Redo Map Edit** re-applies the last undone map edit. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds it to Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y, and the **History** tab can jump forward. Save-point tracking survives redo.
reviews.limitation: The CLI has no persisted undo session to redo into. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Y as a second shortcut for **Redo Map Edit**, alongside Ctrl+Shift+Z. VibeStudio needs no separate command id.
reviews.limitation: The second binding exists only as profile data. The profile test checks every profile for shortcut conflicts but does not assert that Ctrl+Y reaches Redo Map Edit in the NRC profile. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Reload** button on the 3D preview strip invalidates the preview's asset cache and reloads material images and placed models from the package and staged changes. The Models, Sounds and Prefabs browsers each have their own reload button. `map materials` resolves materials and placed models afresh on every CLI run.
reviews.limitation: There is no single command, palette entry or key. One reload does not refresh the preview, the browsers and the entity definitions together, and changed asset files are not watched. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a map.reloadAssets command that clears the preview cache, the asset browsers and the loaded entity definitions in one cancellable task. reviews.workflow: **Repeat Transforms** (Ctrl+R in the NetRadiant Custom profile; **Edit** > **Repeat**, the **Tools** tab and command search) keeps the last move, rotation, scale (a resize or mirror) and shear made on objects or picked components, each replaced only by the next of its kind and kept across selection changes and undo. With objects selected it copies them where they stand, then scales, shears and turns the copies about their centre and moves them, as one undo step named after what it repeated, leaving the copies selected so repeated presses build an array. In Edit Vertices, Edit Edges or Edit Faces it applies the same transforms to the picked components as one Affine component transform about their centre or the component pivot, with Lock Component UVs. **Reset Repeat Transforms** forgets them. `map repeat-transforms` names the transforms on the command line (--scale, --shear, --rotate, --translate; --object or --set). **Repeat Last Commands** (`map repeat`) is unchanged.
reviews.limitation: The object-mode pivot is the centre of the copies' bounds (or --pivot on the CLI), not a user-placed manipulator pivot. Scale, shear, rotation and translation apply in that order, which matches NetRadiant Custom whenever shear and rotation are not both recorded. Quake-family text maps only; Doom maps keep Repeat Last Commands. NetRadiant Custom's Alt+R (Reset Transforms) is left to the menu and palette. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate 90° Left** turns the selection a quarter turn anticlockwise in the active view, using upstream's axis and sign for each view. reviews.limitation: The suggested name differs from NRC, which offers the current name. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Save Region As…** writes the kept objects as a map of their own. Six 16-unit brushes just outside the box seal it: common/caulk in Quake III, the chosen material otherwise. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: `map copy --object … --output fragment.map` writes the selected entities, brushes and patches as a .map fragment, keeping brush-entity ownership and complete groups. Keep the status tag for screen readers.

Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance would remain open once built. Add a persisted 3D Work Zone toggle to the level display options and palette, keep it legible in high-contrast themes, and add an offscreen render test.

reviews.workflow: **Add Patch…** opens the patch editor with a plane at the view centre, square to the active plan view. Choose **Orientation**, **Columns** and **Rows** (3 to 31) and the sizes, then **Generate Shape**. **Patch Plane** on the Levels **Shapes** tab draws a 3x3 plane across a box's top, or replaces selected brushes with one. `map add-patch --shape plane --columns N --rows M` scripts it.

Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Fit Add Patch… to the selection's bounds, with an option to replace the selection, and seed it with the Textures material. Expose Columns and Rows for Patch Plane in the Shapes tab. Apply planar (Align to Face) mapping on creation, and bind Shift+P in the NetRadiant Custom profile.

reviews.workflow: **Smooth Patch Columns** moves each joint along the rows halfway between its neighbours and keeps a closed row closed across its seam, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op smooth-columns` does the same. The NetRadiant Custom profile binds Ctrl+Shift+W.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio wraps only patches at least five columns wide. The CLI route has no automated test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Smooth Patch Rows** moves each joint down the columns halfway between its neighbours, wrapping across a closed seam with the same one-unit test, as one undo step. It is in the Tools tab's **Patch Rows and Columns** group, the Geometry and context menus, and the patch editor's **Rows and Columns** menu. `map patch-matrix --op smooth-rows` does the same.
reviews.limitation: Ctrl+W is not bound in the NetRadiant Custom profile, because **Close Package** keeps it window-wide. VibeStudio wraps only patches at least five rows tall. Only the column variant is checked in core; the UI test only checks that the row command is named and explained, and the CLI route is untested. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Round Selection to Grid** (NRC profile Ctrl+G; Tools tab Transform group, Edit menu, right-click Transform submenu, palette) rounds each brush vertex (including the brushes and patches of selected brush entities), patch control point and point-entity origin of the selection onto the grid in one undo step, through the shared component transform service with component UV lock. In Edit Vertices, Edges or Faces it rounds only the picked components, including faces picked by Select Textured, all or nothing. It runs as a cancellable placement task. Hidden objects, worldspawn and brushes the grid would collapse are left as they were, with their reasons; scene locks and the open group refuse the whole edit. **Snap Selection to Grid** still moves whole objects by their reference point and keeps Ctrl+G in the GtkRadiant and NetRadiant profiles. **Snap Vertices to Grid** remains TrenchBroom's brush-only command. CLI: `map round-to-grid` with `--object` or `--set`, `--grid`, `--uv-lock` and `--context`.
reviews.limitation: In face mode, NRC snaps the picked face's plane points; VibeStudio rounds the face's corners. NRC silently keeps a brush that would degenerate; VibeStudio reports it as skipped. Brush-entity origin keys are left alone (NRC rounds Doom 3 group origins). Doom-format maps fall back to Snap Selection to Grid. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Surfaces** sidebar tab (**Show Surfaces**; titled **Surface** in Radiant-family profiles, NetRadiant Custom included) stays docked with step amounts and one-click shift, rotate, scale, fit, flip, justify, Natural and Align to Face, plus surface copy and paste. The **Inspector** edits a face's texture, shift, rotation and scale or primitive matrix, and **Surface Alignment…** previews a batch. `map edit` and `map align-textures` cover the CLI.
reviews.limitation: No command toggles a surface window: **Show Surfaces** only opens the tab, the NetRadiant Custom profile binds nothing to S, and Radiant 1.4/1.5 and Q3Radiant profiles bind S to the modal, brush-face-only **Surface Alignment…** dialog. Content and surface flags and value cannot be edited per face, only carried by copy and paste, and there are no projection buttons. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Let **Show Surfaces** toggle the tab and bind it to S in the NetRadiant Custom profile, keeping the dialog as the batch preview. Add per-face content and surface flag and value fields with game flag names for Quake II and Quake III faces, and projection buttons once a direction projection exists.
