reviews.workflow: No filter kind reads the nodraw flag. Choose **Select by Texture…** with the game's nodraw texture, or type `texture:nodraw` in the **Objects** filter and press Enter, then **Hide Selection**; **Show All Hidden** brings them back. `map find` lists the same objects. On Quake II maps the **Clip** and **Triggers** filters hide most nodraw brushes.
reviews.limitation: Matching uses texture names on any face, not the 0x80 flag or a Quake III shader's surfaceparm nodraw, and hiding acts on a one-off selection rather than a toggle that re-reads the map. **Filters** has no Nodraw kind. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a Nodraw filter kind with counts, a palette toggle and a CLI report. It should match the 0x80 surface flag on Quake II faces, surfaceparm nodraw from the material library for Quake III, and nodraw texture names.

reviews.workflow: The **Checklist** on the Levels **Map** tab reports player and deathmatch starts, lights, the worldspawn message and wad keys, entity definitions, leaks and Health errors; rows that need work lead to the fix. `entity validate` checks classes, keys, spawnflag bits and target links against a definition catalogue, and `map inspect` prints validation lines.
reviews.limitation: The rules are UFO: Alien Invasion game rules: storey limits, team and civilian starts, and coloured lights. They have no meaning for Doom, Quake, Quake II or Quake III maps, and VibeStudio does not target UFO:AI. No UFO:AI rules are checked. Unlike the plugin, which clamps maxlevel, VibeStudio never rewrites keys during a check. The Checklist has no palette entry and no dedicated automated test.

reviews.workflow: None. The **Filters** section of the **View** tab offers only idTech1–3 kinds and does not read a stepon content.
reviews.limitation: Stepon is a UFO: Alien Invasion movement content. The bit is unused by Quake II brushes and is CONTENTS_TRIGGER in Quake III, where trigger volumes are entities that the Triggers filter already covers by class. VibeStudio does not target UFO:AI. UFO:AI content bits are neither recognised nor filterable.

reviews.workflow: Unticking **Clip** in the **Filters** section of the **View** tab hides brushes whose every face uses a texture named *clip*. That catches Quake III's common/weapclip, along with player and monster clip.
reviews.limitation: 0x2000000 is CONTENTS_MONSTER in Quake II and CONTENTS_BODY in Quake III. These are contents of live entities, not brushes, so the flag test means nothing on idTech2/3 maps. Quake III weapon clip is a shader, common/weapclip, not a unique bit; hiding clip generally is reviewed under nrc:FilterClips. Weapon clip cannot be hidden apart from other clip, and UFO:AI's content bit is not read.

reviews.workflow: The **Worldspawn** section of the Levels **Map** tab edits worldspawn keys, and **Add Key…** suggests common keys and those of the worldspawn definition. Undo puts a change back. `map edit` sets keys from the CLI and writes a separate save-as file.
reviews.limitation: maxlevel and maxteams are UFO: Alien Invasion worldspawn keys for storeys and teams. Doom, Quake, Quake II and Quake III worldspawn has no such keys or derivable defaults, and VibeStudio does not target UFO:AI. Nothing derives default values from map contents, such as counting starts or inferring teams. Keys are entered by hand or picked from suggestions, and the section has no palette entry.

reviews.workflow: Edit or replace values in the **Worldspawn** section of the Levels **Map** tab, or in the **Inspector** after **Select Worldspawn**. Undo puts a change back. `map edit` overwrites keys from the CLI and writes a separate save-as file.
reviews.limitation: maxlevel and maxteams are UFO: Alien Invasion worldspawn keys for storeys and teams. Doom, Quake, Quake II and Quake III worldspawn has no such keys or derivable defaults, and VibeStudio does not target UFO:AI. No command resets worldspawn keys to values computed from the map. Each key is changed explicitly.

reviews.workflow: There is no UFO:AI command set. The generic pieces map to existing routes: the **Clip** filter and **Hide Selection** for clip and nodraw brushes, regions for slicing by height, the **Checklist** and `entity validate` for pre-build checks, and the **Worldspawn** section or `map edit` for keys. Game-specific tools would arrive as extension manifests.
reviews.limitation: The provider exists for UFO: Alien Invasion, which VibeStudio does not target, and depends on Radiant's plugin interface. Its two generic behaviours, hiding nodraw and player clip brushes, are reviewed under the NoDraw and ActorClip entries. There is no Radiant plugin compatibility, no UFO:AI game profile or toolbar, and no UFO:AI content-flag names, storey filters or entity rules.

reviews.limitation: This is a developer template. Its console output is fixed, it changes nothing in the map, and NRC does not even build it. VibeStudio has no in-process Radiant plugin API, so a mapper gains nothing from an equivalent. Not applicable. VibeStudio deliberately offers no plugin interface compatible with Radiant's.

reviews.workflow: **Surface Alignment** shifts, scales, rotates, fits and aligns brush faces with numeric values and a material preview. **Edit Patch Control Points** has a per-point UV table, **Reset UV** and a UV checker preview. `map align-textures` and `map edit-patch` make the same edits from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: There is no interactive texture-space view. Face windings and patch control points cannot be dragged over the texture image, and there is no anchor-point rotation with live camera feedback; edits are numeric or per point. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a UV view for one picked face or patch. It should draw the winding or control grid over the material image, support point drag, anchor rotation, zoom, pan and keyboard nudges, preview in the camera, and commit one undo step through the surface and patch services.

reviews.workflow: UV work is spread over **Surface Alignment**, which edits face mapping numerically with a preview, and **Edit Patch Control Points**, which has a per-point UV table and a UV checker. The CLI equivalents are `map align-textures` and `map edit-patch`. The manual covers help.
reviews.limitation: There is no drag-in-texture-space editor with anchor rotation or live camera feedback. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build the interactive face/patch UV view described for Go...; About and Help need no counterpart.

reviews.workflow: Escape in a 2D view cancels a drag, drops a draft and leaves draw, clip, shear, shape and region modes, then clears face picks and finally the selection. In the camera it cancels moves, mouse look, component and surface tools, and picked faces. **Select None** and **Close Group** are separate commands; Radiant-style profiles bind Escape to **Select None**.
reviews.limitation: Escape is hard-coded in the views rather than a bindable command. The camera never clears whole-object selections, and Escape does not close an open group when nothing is selected. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Route Escape through a bindable map.cancel command in TrenchBroom's order: run the view's cancel cascade, then deselect in either view, then close the open group.

reviews.workflow: **Draw Brush in Camera** drags a box footprint on an XY, XZ or YZ construction plane, which **Use Camera Surface** can place on the surface at the camera centre; the wheel sets depth. **Add Brush…** and `map add-brush` preview primitives from bounds. **Wrap/Merge** wraps picked vertices, edges or faces into a new hull, and **Wrap/Merge with Points…** and `map wrap-merge` add up to three XYZ points. Active clip points also join the hull.
reviews.limitation: There is no free point-cloud tool: you cannot click grid-snapped points on surfaces and press Return to get a hull. Wrap/Merge needs source brushes or picked components and takes at most three extra points, and camera drawing makes boxes only. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add an Assemble Brush camera tool. Clicks on surfaces add grid-snapped points, a face drag or Shift-drag extrudes, and the convex hull previews asynchronously. Return creates one brush with the current material in one undo step. Lift the three-point cap for this route and add a CLI hull-from-points route, for example `map add-brush --point` repeated.

reviews.workflow: **Cycle Map View** steps a single view through 3D, Top, Front and Side. When the camera sits beside a 2D view, it steps the 2D view through its planes. The TrenchBroom profile binds Space, which applies on the Levels page and is left to the focused control elsewhere.
reviews.limitation: Unlike TrenchBroom, the newly shown view is not framed on the selection; use Frame Selection afterwards. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Select** tool at the head of the level authoring bar ends clip, vertex, edge and face editing, Draw Sector, shape and Make Sector modes and the camera's brush, paint and sample tools in one click. Each tool also turns off from its own command: **Clip Tool**, **Sweep Tool**, **Shear Tool**, **Edit Vertices**, **Edit Edges** and **Edit Faces** toggle. Escape leaves a tool once its draft or picks are cleared.
reviews.limitation: The Select tool has no command id, palette entry or shortcut, and it leaves the shear, sweep and region tools running. Escape may need several presses, and nothing is bound to Shift+Escape. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Make the Select tool also end shear, sweep and region drawing, register it as a map.deactivate-tool palette command that reports which tool closed, and bind Shift+Escape in the TrenchBroom profile.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Duplicate and move objects backward; Duplicate and move objects up
reviews.workflow: **Duplicate and Move Depth Up** (Ctrl+Page Up in the TrenchBroom profile; **Edit** > **Duplicate and Move**, the **Tools** tab and command search) copies the selection and moves the copies one grid step towards the viewer along the plan view's depth axis, or up world Z from the camera, as one undo step and one Repeat Last Commands entry, with the copies selected so the next press copies the copies. Texture Lock, scene locks and the open group apply. `map nudge --direction depth-up --duplicate` does the same from the CLI; **Duplicate with Offset…** and `map duplicate --delta` remain for exact offsets and arrays.
reviews.limitation: Quake-family maps only: on Doom maps the command is disabled and Ctrl+Page Up keeps raising ceilings. Copies whole objects only, so it is disabled in Edit Vertices, Edit Edges and Edit Faces and while the Sweep Tool is on. Only the TrenchBroom profile binds the key; other profiles reach it from the menu, Tools tab or palette. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Horizontal** mirrors the selection along the active plan view's horizontal axis or, from the camera, along its right axis snapped to a world axis. It is one undo step that honours **Texture Lock** and Valve 220 conversion settings, Doom and UDMF geometry included. The TrenchBroom profile mirrors about the selection centre rounded to half the grid while **Snap** is on (`editing.flipSnapsPivot` for any profile), so an on-grid selection flips in place. That profile binds <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd>, which the views claim only while the flip can act, so Find keeps Ctrl+F everywhere else. Flips are disabled while the **Sweep Tool** is on. CLI: `map view-transform --transform flip-horizontal [--pivot-grid N]`, or `map flip --axis` for a world axis.
reviews.limitation: TrenchBroom disables flips for every modal tool. VibeStudio disables them only while Sweep is on: it flips picked components in vertex, edge and face modes, and still flips in the clip tool. With nothing selected, Ctrl+F in a view focuses search. NetRadiant Custom's full-grid flip pivot is not reproduced; that profile flips about the exact centre. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip Vertical** mirrors along the active plan view's vertical axis (Y from the top, Z from the front and side) or, from the camera, along world Z. It is one undo step with **Texture Lock**, using the TrenchBroom profile's half-grid pivot while **Snap** is on. That profile binds <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>F</kbd>, claimed only by the views while the flip can act. Flips are disabled while the **Sweep Tool** is on. CLI: `map view-transform --transform flip-vertical`, or `map flip --axis` for a world axis, including Doom and UDMF geometry.
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio disables flips only during Sweep, where TrenchBroom disables them for every modal tool. Doom maps refuse the camera's Z flip. NetRadiant Custom's full-grid flip pivot is not reproduced. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Flip U** on the Levels **Surfaces** tab mirrors the Surfaces target's U axis (a scale of −1 about the middle) as one undo step, for brushes, picked faces and patches. **Surface Alignment…** with a Scale of −1 on X does the same for chosen faces, and `map align-textures --flip u` matches it in the CLI.
reviews.limitation: Flip U acts on the texture's U axis, not the camera's horizontal, so on rotated textures or floors seen from another angle it can flip a different axis from TB. No profile binds Ctrl+F (the global Find key), and Flip U has no palette entry. Only a patch flip has an automated test; brush-face flips and the button have none. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add camera-relative flip commands that choose U or V from the camera's right and up vectors, as TB's flipUV does. Register palette entries and bind Ctrl+F in the TrenchBroom profile's camera context. Add core and UI tests for brush-face flips.

reviews.workflow: **Flip V** on the Levels **Surfaces** tab mirrors the Surfaces target's V axis (a scale of −1 about the middle) as one undo step, for brushes, picked faces and patches. **Surface Alignment…** with a Scale of −1 on Y does the same for chosen faces, and `map align-textures --flip v` matches it.
reviews.limitation: Flip V uses the texture's V axis rather than the camera's vertical, so results can differ from TB on rotated textures or views. No profile binds Ctrl+Alt+F, and Flip V has no palette entry. Only a patch U flip is tested; V flips and the button have no automated test. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a camera-relative vertical flip that picks U or V from the camera's up vector. Register a palette entry, bind Ctrl+Alt+F in the TrenchBroom profile and add core and UI tests.

reviews.workflow: In the TrenchBroom profile, Make Structural (Alt+S; Geometry menu, Tools > Brush, right-click Transform, palette) clears the detail flag and moves the selected brushes out of any brush entity to the world, into the open group or current layer, as one undo step. It is refused when nothing would change. Other profiles keep the detail-only policy, which now takes only the selected brushes out of a func_detail. `map detail --structural --policy trenchbroom` (or `detail`) matches it, and the policy appears in the profile's controls reference.
reviews.limitation: Only the detail content flag is cleared; TrenchBroom's other smart tags (liquid, transparency and other flag tags) are not. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Move objects backward; Move objects up
reviews.workflow: **Nudge Depth Up** (TrenchBroom profile: Page Up) moves one grid step towards the viewer along a plan view's depth axis (Top +Z, Front -Y, Side +X), or up world Z from the camera. It moves the sweep destination, the component pivot, picked components or the selection, as one undo step with Texture Lock, scene locks and open-group context. On Doom maps the depth nudges are disabled, so Page Up still runs Raise Floor. The command is remappable and in the palette, Edit > Nudge and the Tools tab. `map nudge --direction depth-up --view front` works headlessly.
reviews.limitation: Profiles other than TrenchBroom leave the depth nudges unbound by default. Out-of-plane split and extrusion component nudges are refused. UI coverage uses synthetic offscreen key events. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Move objects down; Move objects backward
reviews.workflow: **Nudge Back** (TrenchBroom profile: Down) moves one grid step down the screen in a plan view, or back along the horizontal world axis nearest the camera's view in 3D, including from the single 3D layout. Like every nudge it moves the sweep destination, the component pivot, picked components or the selection, whichever is active first, as one undo step with Texture Lock, scene locks and open-group context. Shift moves eight steps. The command is remappable and in the palette, Edit > Nudge and the Tools tab. `map nudge --direction back` works headlessly.
reviews.limitation: The Rotate Selection dialog's pivot is not nudged. Split and extrusion component nudges stay in a plan view's plane. UI coverage uses synthetic offscreen key events. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Move objects forward; Move objects down
reviews.workflow: **Nudge Depth Down** (TrenchBroom profile: Page Down) moves one grid step away from the viewer along a plan view's depth axis, or down world Z from the camera. It moves the sweep destination, the component pivot, picked components or the selection, as one undo step with Texture Lock, scene locks and open-group context. Doom maps keep Page Down for Lower Floor. The command is remappable and in the palette, Edit > Nudge and the Tools tab. `map nudge --direction depth-down` works headlessly.
reviews.limitation: Profiles other than TrenchBroom leave the depth nudges unbound by default. Out-of-plane split and extrusion component nudges are refused. UI coverage uses synthetic offscreen key events. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Nudge Left** (TrenchBroom profile: Left) moves one grid step left in a plan view, or along the camera's negated right axis snapped to the nearest world axis in 3D (turned a quarter about Z if it would equal Forward). It moves the sweep destination, the component pivot, picked components or the selection, whichever is active first, as one undo step with Texture Lock, scene locks and open-group context. reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Move objects up; Move objects forward
reviews.workflow: **Nudge Forward** (Edit > Nudge, Tools > Nudge, command search; TrenchBroom profile: Up) moves one grid step: up the screen in a plan view, or forward along the horizontal world axis nearest the camera's view in 3D (the camera's up axis when it looks straight down or up). The TrenchBroom single 3D layout nudges without cycling to a 2D view. It moves the sweep destination while the Sweep Tool is on, the component pivot under Rotate Components or Move Component Pivot, picked vertices, edges or faces in component modes, and otherwise the selection, as one undo step with Texture Lock, scene locks and open-group context. Shift moves eight steps. Keys are remappable in Keyboard Shortcuts. `map nudge --direction forward` takes a --view or --camera-yaw/--camera-pitch frame headlessly.
reviews.limitation: The Rotate Selection dialog's pivot is not nudged; only the component pivot stands in for TB's rotation centre. Split and extrusion component nudges stay in a plan view's plane and are refused from the camera. UI coverage uses synthetic offscreen key events. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Levels → Surfaces** **V −** (Shift Texture V −) shifts the selection or picked faces by the **Shift step** (default 8 texels) through the shared surface edit queue, as an undoable edit. The GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5, Q3Radiant and QeRadiant profiles bind it to Shift+Down in the level views. CLI: `map align-textures --shift 0,-N`.
reviews.limitation: TrenchBroom moves against the camera's projected up vector by the grid size. VibeStudio shifts along texture V by a session step, so on rotated or sideways faces the direction can differ. The TrenchBroom profile binds no key: its camera leaves the arrows unbound and its 2D views use them to nudge objects. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add camera-relative texture moves that project the camera vectors onto each face's UV axes and step by the grid size. Bind plain Down in the TrenchBroom camera only while faces are selected; keep object nudging otherwise.

reviews.workflow: Uses the same route as the normal move. Set the **Shift step** to twice the grid size, then use **V −** (Shift Texture V −) on the selection or picked faces. CLI: `map align-textures --shift 0,-N` takes any amount.
reviews.limitation: There is no one-key coarse command. TrenchBroom's Shift+Down moves twice the grid size against the camera's up vector; VibeStudio needs the step edited and shifts along texture V. In the GtkRadiant, Q3Radiant and QeRadiant profiles Shift+Down is the ordinary step. TrenchBroom-profile bindings, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Once the camera-relative base move exists, add a coarse command (twice the grid size) and bind Shift+Down in the TrenchBroom camera while faces are selected.

reviews.workflow: Set the **Shift step** to 1, then use **V −** (Shift Texture V −), or run `map align-textures --shift 0,-1`. **Surface Alignment…** also takes exact offsets. On Doom walls, **Nudge Texture Down at Crosshair** slides the sidedef offset by one unit.
reviews.limitation: There is no one-key fine command for brush faces. TrenchBroom's Ctrl+Down moves one unit against the camera's up vector; VibeStudio shifts along texture V by the session step. The Doom crosshair nudge covers only wall sidedefs and has no palette entry. TrenchBroom-profile bindings, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Once the camera-relative base move exists, add a fine command (one unit) and bind Ctrl+Down in the TrenchBroom camera while faces are selected.

reviews.workflow: **Pitch Clockwise** (<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Page Up</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile; also in **Edit** > **Transform**, the **Tools** tab and command search) turns the selection 90° clockwise about the view's right axis. That axis runs across the active plan view, or is the camera's right axis snapped to a world axis (turned a quarter about Z when it would coincide with forward). It is one undo step with Texture Lock, pivoting on the grid-rounded selection centre in the TrenchBroom and NetRadiant Custom profiles while **Snap** is on. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination by the rotation step. CLI: `map view-transform --transform pitch-clockwise`.
reviews.limitation: No Rotate-tool angle or centre, so a pitch is always 90°. The key acts while a Levels view has focus. Doom maps refuse pitch. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Pitch Counter-clockwise** (<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Page Down</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile) turns 90° counter-clockwise about the view's right axis: across the plan view, or the camera's snapped right axis. It is one undo step with Texture Lock and the profile's quick-turn pivot. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination. CLI: `map view-transform --transform pitch-counterclockwise`.
reviews.limitation: No Rotate-tool angle or centre. The key acts while a Levels view has focus. Doom maps refuse pitch. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **View** > **Camera** > **Reset Camera Zoom** (<kbd>Ctrl+Alt+Z</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile; also **Tools** > **Navigate** and command search) returns the 3D camera's field of view to the active profile's after a <kbd>Shift</kbd>+wheel zoom or a saved view's own field of view. The camera keeps its place and mouse look resumes if it was on. A second press only reports that the profile's field of view is already in use.
reviews.limitation: A pure view command with no CLI route. The reset goes through the shared viewport's state restore, which ends mouse look; the shell restarts it, so a held mouse-look gesture begins again. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Natural** on the Surfaces tab resets the target to zero shift and rotation at the format's natural scale (0.5 in Quake III, 1 otherwise), square to the world. **Align to Face** resets along the face's own plane. Both are one undo step, handle patches too, and match `map align-textures --natural` or `--face-aligned`.
reviews.limitation: No single reset keeps each face's current projection kind and uses game-configuration defaults; the user picks Natural or Align to Face. Neither command has a palette entry or TB's Shift+R binding. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a map.surfaceReset command that resets offsets, rotation and scale to the game's defaults while keeping each face's projection kind. Register palette entries for it, Natural and Align to Face, and bind Shift+R in the TrenchBroom profile.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/Reset texture alignment to world aligned
reviews.workflow: **Natural** on the Levels **Surfaces** tab resets the target to zero shift and rotation at the format's natural scale, projected square to the world, as Radiant's Natural does, in classic, Valve 220 and brush-primitive faces. It also gives patches natural texturing, in one undo step. `map align-textures --natural U,V` matches it.
reviews.limitation: Natural uses the format's natural scale rather than a per-game configuration default. The TrenchBroom profile does not bind Shift+Alt+R. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Reveal Material** (Edit, Tools > Surfaces, the Surfaces menu above the views, the object right-click menu and command search) reads the picked faces and query-picked patches, or else the selected brushes, patches, entities, Doom lines and sectors. When they share one material it shows the **Textures** tab, clears a filter that hides the tile, selects and scrolls to it, and makes it the current material for painting and new brushes. A mixed selection disables the command; its status tip, tooltip and the Tools-tab button's accessible description name two of the materials. As in TrenchBroom and NetRadiant Custom, no profile gives it a key. **Sample Map Material** (`map sample-material`) still takes a clicked camera surface's material.
reviews.limitation: Reveal has no CLI route because it changes only the view and the current material. TrenchBroom's camera context-menu item for the face under the pointer ('Reveal <material> in Material Browser', 'Copy Material Name') is not added; the plan view's object menu carries the command instead. Native physical input, screen readers and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Select objects (or pick components) and use **Roll Clockwise**: **Edit** > **Transform**, the **Transform** menu, the **Tools** tab or command search, or <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Up</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile. It turns the selection 90° clockwise, as seen looking along the view's forward axis, as one undo step with Texture Lock. The forward axis is up the active plan view (Y from the top, Z from the front and side), or the horizontal world axis nearest the camera's view. While **Snap** is on, the TrenchBroom and NetRadiant Custom profiles pivot on the grid point nearest the selection centre. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination by the rotation step instead (15° by default). `map view-transform --transform roll-clockwise --view top|front|side` or `--camera-yaw/--camera-pitch`, with optional `--pivot-grid N`, does the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: TrenchBroom's Rotate-tool angle and centre have no counterpart (VibeStudio has no object rotate tool), so a roll is always 90°. The key acts while a Levels view has focus; from menus and command search, the last focused view decides. The Radiant-family cameras use the last plan view's axes. Doom maps refuse roll. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Roll Counter-clockwise** (<kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Down</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile; also in **Edit** > **Transform**, the **Tools** tab and command search) turns the selection 90° counter-clockwise about the view's forward axis. That axis is up the active plan view, or the horizontal world axis nearest the camera's view. It is one undo step with Texture Lock, using the profile's grid-rounded quick-turn pivot while **Snap** is on. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination instead. CLI: `map view-transform --transform roll-counterclockwise`.
reviews.limitation: No Rotate-tool angle or centre, so a roll is always 90°. The key acts only while a Levels view has focus; with nothing selected, Alt+Down reaches the view, which pans. Doom maps refuse roll. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Levels → Surfaces** **Rotate +** (Rotate Texture +) turns the targeted faces and patches by the **Rotation step** about each face centre, as an undoable edit. The default step of 15° matches TrenchBroom's grid angle. The GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5, Q3Radiant and QeRadiant profiles bind Shift+Page Down. CLI: `map align-textures --degrees N`.
reviews.limitation: TrenchBroom binds Page Up in the camera; the TrenchBroom profile has no binding, and VibeStudio's step is an editable session value rather than a fixed angle. Rotate + uses the same positive sign as TrenchBroom's and Radiant's clockwise commands, but visual clockwise parity across classic, Valve 220 and brush-primitive faces is unverified. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a fixed 15-degree clockwise texture rotation command that does not depend on the panel step, and bind Page Up to it in the TrenchBroom camera while faces are selected. Add a test that confirms the visual clockwise direction for each face format.

reviews.workflow: Set the **Rotation step** to 90°, then use **Rotate +** (Rotate Texture +) on the selection or picked faces. CLI: `map align-textures --degrees 90`.
reviews.limitation: There is no one-key 90-degree command; the step has to be edited. In the GtkRadiant, Q3Radiant and QeRadiant profiles Shift+Page Up runs Rotate − by the ordinary step, which conflicts with the TrenchBroom meaning. Visual direction parity per face format, TrenchBroom-profile bindings, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a fixed 90-degree clockwise texture rotation command and bind Shift+Page Up to it in the TrenchBroom profile only, while faces are selected.

reviews.workflow: Set the **Rotation step** to 1°, then use **Rotate +** (Rotate Texture +) on the selection or picked faces. CLI: `map align-textures --degrees 1`. **Surface Alignment…** also accepts exact angles.
reviews.limitation: There is no one-key one-degree command; the step has to be edited. Visual clockwise parity per face format, a TrenchBroom-profile Ctrl+Page Up binding, native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a fixed one-degree clockwise texture rotation command and bind Ctrl+Page Up to it in the TrenchBroom camera while faces are selected.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate −** on the Levels **Surfaces** tab (**Rotate Texture −** in command search) turns the Surfaces target by the negative **Rotation step**, 15° by default, as one undo step. It covers selected brushes, picked faces and patches. The GtkRadiant 1.4/1.5 and Q3Radiant profiles bind it to Radiant's anticlockwise Shift+PgUp. **Surface Alignment…** and `map align-textures --degrees -N` take exact angles.
reviews.limitation: The TrenchBroom profile binds no Page Down key, and the step comes from the Surfaces panel, not a grid rotation angle. VibeStudio pivots each face about its centre, so the resulting offsets can differ from TB's. Only the core and CLI rotate paths are tested; the button and keys have no UI test. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Bind Page Down to map.surfaceRotateLeft in the TrenchBroom profile, scoped to the camera. Optionally take the default step from a level rotation-snap angle, and offer a TB-style rotation that does not re-centre the face. Add a UI test for the rotate buttons and keys.

reviews.workflow: Set the Surfaces tab's **Rotation step** to 90° and press **Rotate −**. You can also enter −90 in **Surface Alignment…** (Rotate) or run `map align-textures --degrees -90`. Each is one undo step on the Surfaces target.
reviews.limitation: No coarse command exists, so the user changes the shared step or types an angle. No profile binds Shift+Page Down to a coarse turn; in the Radiant profiles it already turns the other way by the normal step. Rotation is centre-anchored, unlike TB. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add fixed 90° coarse rotate commands (map.surfaceRotateLeftCoarse and its clockwise pair) with palette entries. Bind Shift+Page Down to them in the TrenchBroom profile and cover them in the quick-surface UI test.

reviews.workflow: Set the Surfaces tab's **Rotation step** to 1° (it accepts down to 0.001°) and press **Rotate −**. You can also enter −1 in **Surface Alignment…** or run `map align-textures --degrees -1`. Each is one undo step on the Surfaces target.
reviews.limitation: There is no fine command alongside the normal step, so switching step sizes means editing the spin box. No profile binds Ctrl+Page Down. Rotation is centre-anchored, unlike TB. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add fixed 1° fine rotate commands with palette entries. Bind Ctrl+Page Down in the TrenchBroom profile and add UI coverage.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Hide entity links
reviews.workflow: Unticking **Target Links** hides every link that does not touch the selection. The selection's own links are always drawn in the 2D views. The camera draws no links at all. Existing control: Show menu > Target Links unticked (levelMapShowLinks); View tab checkbox (levelViewShowLinks)
reviews.limitation: No setting also hides the selection's links, the toggle has no palette entry or shortcut, and it is hidden on Doom maps. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a none link mode that also suppresses the selection's links, exposed through the shared link-mode commands and the Show menu, including on Doom maps.

reviews.workflow: **View** > **3D Wireframe** draws the level camera as edges instead of faces, so you can see what lies behind. The same toggle is on the **View** sidebar tab and in the palette. The VibeStudio profile binds W; the TrenchBroom, Radiant and other familiar profiles leave it unbound, as TrenchBroom does.
reviews.limitation: It is a single unsaved toggle, not TrenchBroom's persistent face mode: the camera returns to textured or flat shading whenever the preview rebuilds, for example after an edit, and turning it off ignores the Textures choice. It draws every render triangle's edges, not brush polygon edges. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Keep wireframe across preview rebuilds and restore the previous textured or flat mode when it is turned off. Offer an explicit, persisted face mode (textured, flat, hidden) that profiles can bind.

reviews.workflow: Untick **Textures** above the level views, or the matching **Textures in Camera** checkbox on the **View** sidebar tab, and the camera draws flat-shaded faces. Ticking it brings back package images and static shader previews. The choice is kept in the shell layout state. Existing control: Textures checkbox in the level preview status strip above the views (levelPreviewTextured); View tab checkbox (levelViewTextured)
reviews.limitation: The toggle is a plain QAction with no command id, so it is not in the palette and takes no profile or user shortcut. Turning 3D Wireframe off returns to flat shading until the preview next rebuilds, and the status-strip box does not follow a change made on the View tab. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Register the textures toggle as a palette command (for example map.preview-textures), with explicit show and hide entries that profiles can bind, keep both checkboxes in sync, and make 3D Wireframe restore the Textures choice when it is turned off.

reviews.workflow: No equivalent toggle. The level camera always shades flat and textured faces with a Lambert term from a camera-relative light, matching TrenchBroom's default state, so faces pointing different ways read apart. No command turns this shading off. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Shading is permanently on. Faces cannot be shown unshaded for a material or flat-colour check, and no profile can bind a toggle. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open once a toggle is built. Remaining work: Add a uniform flag that skips the Lambert factor in model_surface.vert for both backends. Add a persisted Shade Faces toggle on the View tab and a palette command, then regenerate the shader data.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Show all entity links
reviews.workflow: **Show** > **Target Links**, on by default and also on the **View** tab, draws arrows for every target and killtarget link in the 2D views, dashed for killtargets; Doom maps draw every tag link in the Top view. `map render --links` draws Quake-family target links into an SVG, and `map inspect` reports them as targetLinks.
reviews.limitation: Links are drawn only in the 2D views, not in the camera. The toggle has no command id, palette entry or shortcut, and it is hidden on Doom maps, where tag-link display cannot be switched. `map render --links` omits Doom tag links. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Replace the boolean with a link display mode (all, transitive, direct, none) that also applies to Doom tag links, expose each mode as a palette command, and draw links in the level camera as well.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Show directly selected entity links
reviews.workflow: Untick **Show** > **Target Links**, or the **View** tab checkbox. The 2D views then draw only the target, killtarget and Doom tag links that touch the selection, emphasised, and the viewport description says links are shown for the selection only. Existing control: Show menu > Target Links unticked (levelMapShowLinks); View tab checkbox (levelViewShowLinks)
reviews.limitation: Links are not drawn in the camera, and the toggle has no command id, palette entry or shortcut. It is hidden on Doom maps, so tag links cannot be narrowed there. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Expose direct mode as an explicit, bindable link-mode command within a shared link display mode, offer it on Doom maps, and draw the selection's links in the level camera.

reviews.workflow: No direct equivalent. The level camera outlines only selected or hovered objects, and 3D Wireframe shows edges without faces. ModelViewport already supports an edge overlay, used by the Models workbench and level dialog previews such as the brush editor, but the level camera never enables it. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Brush boundaries on faces with similar shading are hard to read in the camera, and no profile can bind an edge toggle. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open once a toggle is built. Remaining work: Add a persisted Edges in Camera toggle that calls ModelViewport::setShowEdges on the level camera, with a palette command and a View tab checkbox. Make sure brush polygon edges are drawn rather than triangulation diagonals.

reviews.workflow: The **Textures** check box in the camera's preview status bar, mirrored as **Textures in Camera** on the **View** tab, switches the camera between textured and flat-shaded rendering. The choice is remembered. **3D Wireframe** draws edges only. Existing control: Level camera preview status bar > Textures check box; View tab > Textures in Camera
reviews.limitation: The control is a check box with no command id, so it cannot be bound or found in command search. It affects only the camera; the 2D views draw outlines. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Show transitively selected entity links
reviews.workflow: No transitive display mode. With **Target Links** on, every link is drawn, the selection's chains among the rest. With it off, the 2D views show only links touching the selection, so repeating **Select Connected Entities** grows the selection one hop at a time and brings each next link into view. `map select-connected` returns the same direct connections for scripts.
reviews.limitation: A chain cannot be isolated without changing the selection, there is no bindable link mode, and the camera draws no links. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a transitive link mode that walks levelMapTargetLinks outward from the selected entities, using a visited set to stop cycles. Draw it in the plan views and the camera and expose it as a palette command.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show brush entity bounds
reviews.workflow: Not covered. Brush entities are drawn as their brushes, in the brush-entity colour. The **Brush Entities** filter on the **View** tab hides whole entities, but no bounding boxes are drawn. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: VibeStudio draws no brush-entity bounds, so there is no outline to toggle. Hiding the entities with the filter is a different job. Remaining work: Draw brush-entity bounds in the 2D views and the camera overlay, tinted by class colour where definitions provide one. Put them behind a remembered Show-menu toggle with a command id and add overlay snapshot tests.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show brushes
reviews.workflow: Toggle Brushes with the View tab check box, View > Filters > Brushes, Select > Filters on the view bar, or command search. It hides every brush whatever entity owns it, world or entity, in all views and from picking, and leaves patches to the Patches filter, as TrenchBroom's Show Brushes does. Like TrenchBroom, it has no default key; bind one in Controls. The state is saved, and `map filters` reports the kind.
reviews.limitation: Already-selected brushes stay selected when hidden. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show entity classnames
reviews.workflow: **Labels** in the view bar's **Show** menu, mirrored on the **View** tab, writes each entity's classname beside its diamond marker in the 2D views; Doom things show their type number. The choice is remembered. Existing control: Levels view bar > Show menu > Labels; View tab > Labels check box
reviews.limitation: Labels are drawn only for entities with an origin, only in the 2D views and at most 160 per paint. The camera and origin-less brush entities get no classname labels. The toggle has no command id, so it cannot be bound or found in command search. No automated test checks the labels. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Register a map.toggleLabels command for the existing action. Label brush entities at their bounds centre, add camera labels with the same cap and accessible text, and add an overlay test.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show group bounds
reviews.workflow: Not covered. VibeStudio has closed and open groups and reports the selected or open group in the status bar, but draws no group bounds. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: No group bounds are drawn in either view, so there is nothing to toggle. Remaining work: Draw closed-group bounds, optionally with names, in the 2D views and the camera overlay from scene membership. Put them behind a remembered Show-menu toggle with a command id, respect hidden and filtered members, and add an overlay snapshot test.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show point entities
reviews.workflow: The **Point Entities** check box in the **View** tab's **Filters** section hides every entity without brushes in the 2D views and the camera, with a live count. Selection queries skip filtered objects. **Show Every Kind** restores all filters, and the state is remembered. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Point Entities check box (levelFilter-point-entities)
reviews.limitation: The filter is a check box with no command id, so it cannot be bound to a key or found in command search. No CLI reports filter matches. Viewport masking is tested, but core filter matching and the check box have no dedicated automated test. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show point entity bounds
reviews.workflow: Not covered. Point entities appear in the 2D views as fixed-size diamond markers, and the camera draws only placed models. Entity-definition sizes are parsed and used for placement, pasting and region selection, but never drawn. The **Point Entities** filter hides whole entities, which is a different job. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: No definition-sized point-entity boxes are drawn in any view, so there is nothing to toggle. The Show menu's **Entities** item is documented for these markers, but the 2D paint code checks it only for Doom things. Remaining work: Draw definition-sized point-entity boxes, with a 16-unit fallback, in the 2D views and the camera overlay. Give the boxes a remembered toggle with a command id, separate from the marker and entity toggles, make Show > Entities hide Quake-family markers as documented, and add overlay tests.

reviews.id: tb:Controls/Map view/View Filter > Toggle show point entity models
reviews.workflow: The camera draws placed models for entities with a `model` key, including Quake III misc_model skins and remaps. The **Models** filter on the **View** tab hides misc_model and misc_gamemodel entities in every view. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters > Models check box (levelFilter-models)
reviews.limitation: No toggle hides models while keeping the entities: the Models filter hides whole misc_model entities. Models named only in entity definitions are not drawn at all. There is no command id for binding. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a remembered camera toggle with a command id that leaves model instances out of the preview mesh and draws definition-sized boxes instead. Resolve editor models from entity definitions so the toggle also covers monsters and items.

reviews.workflow: No equivalent. The level camera has no distance fog; depth comes from face shading, perspective and the plan views. Quake III fog shaders appear only as a fog trait in the material library and in the Materials workbench previews. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Large maps cannot be given an editor depth cue, and no profile can bind one. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open once a fog option is built. Remaining work: Add an optional distance-fog term to model_surface.frag for OpenGL and Vulkan, with colour and start/end distances from the camera. Add a persisted Fog toggle on the View tab and a palette command.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate 90° Right** is TrenchBroom's Yaw Clockwise. In a plan view it turns the selection 90° clockwise, as the view shows it, about the axis pointing at the viewer. From the camera (focused, or the only view showing) it turns about world Z, clockwise from above. It is one undo step with Texture Lock, pivoting on the grid-rounded centre in the TrenchBroom and NetRadiant Custom profiles while **Snap** is on (`editing.quickTurnSnapsPivot` for any profile). The TrenchBroom profile binds <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Left</kbd>; the views claim it only while the command can act, so Go Back keeps Alt+Left everywhere else. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination. CLI: `map view-transform --transform yaw-clockwise`, or `map rotate --axis z --turns -1`.
reviews.limitation: No Rotate-tool angle or centre. Radiant-family profiles keep the last plan view's axes from the camera, as NetRadiant Custom does. With nothing selected, Alt+Left in a view still goes back, where TrenchBroom does nothing. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate 90° Left** is TrenchBroom's Yaw Counter-clockwise. It turns 90° counter-clockwise about the plan view's depth axis, or about world Z from the camera, as one undo step with Texture Lock and the profile's quick-turn pivot. It is bound to <kbd>Alt</kbd>+<kbd>Right</kbd> in the TrenchBroom profile, claimed by the views only while it can act, so Go Forward keeps the key elsewhere. While the **Sweep Tool** is on, it turns the sweep destination. CLI: `map view-transform --transform yaw-counterclockwise`, or `map rotate --axis z --turns 1`.
reviews.limitation: No Rotate-tool angle or centre. Radiant-family cameras keep the last plan view's axes. With nothing selected, Alt+Right in a view still goes forward. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Every point and brush class of the loaded entity definitions (worldspawn and base classes aside) has its own **Create** command, such as **Create light** or **Create func_door** (`map.createEntity.<class>`). Find it by name in command search, or give it keys in Keyboard Shortcuts. The commands are registered again whenever the definitions change, and keys given to a class are kept while it is not loaded. A point class goes in at the pointer, or the middle of the view, through the CreateEntity placement operation: its definition box is placed against the plan plane or the brush the camera ray hits, on the grid, as Paste at Cursor places objects. A brush class makes the selected brushes, patches and brushes of selected brush entities into one; it is enabled only once brushes are selected. Each is one undo step and refuses locked, hidden or out-of-group brushes and a locked current layer with the reason. **Create Entity…** types a class in a picker. The Brush Entity right-click menu uses the same bindable commands. CLI: `map create-entity` (also `map add-entity`, `map tie-entity`).
reviews.limitation: Pre-alpha and largely untested in real projects. The plan views place a point class on the plane at their brush depth (or the selection's depth), as Paste at Cursor does; they do not anchor on a selected brush face under the pointer as TrenchBroom's 2D views do. Definition default keys are not filled in. The per-class palette ids are generated at runtime, so `ui semantics` lists only Create Entity, though registry lookups resolve each generated id. A brush class also accepts patches and selected brush entities, and refuses hidden brushes, where TrenchBroom accepts brushes only. No profile binds the commands, as in TrenchBroom. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: The **Filters** on the **View** tab hide whole kinds of entity (lights, triggers, monsters, items, player starts, point or brush entities) and show counts. For one class, **Select All of This Class**, or an Objects filter such as class=info_null with **Select Matching Objects**, then **Hide Selection** hides its current members; **Show All Hidden** brings them back. `map visibility` previews hide and show; `map find --where class=…` lists members.
reviews.limitation: There is no per-class filter and no per-class command to bind. The kind filters are coarse, and hiding by selection does not cover entities of that class added later. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add class filters built from the loaded entity definitions to the View tab Filters, kept for the map session. Generate 'Toggle <class> visible' palette commands that users can bind in editor keys, and add a class option to `map visibility`.

reviews.workflow: The **Filters** section of the Levels **View** tab has a check box for each kind, with counts: detail, clip, hint and skip, caulk, sky, liquids, triggers, lights and more, or the thing categories on a Doom map. Unticking a kind hides it in the 2D views and the camera, separately from objects hidden by hand, and the choice is remembered. **Show Every Kind** brings them all back. Filters never change the map, builds or packages. Existing control: Levels > View tab > Filters section check boxes (levelFilter-<id>) and Show Every Kind (levelFiltersShowAll)
reviews.limitation: The kinds are fixed rules based on texture names, flags and class prefixes, not tags defined by the game. Hint and skip share one filter, and there is no Quake II translucent or Quake III fog kind. Filters are not commands, so they have no keys, palette entries or CLI; the NetRadiant Custom profile lists a Toggle Caulk Filter binding that nothing runs. No test covers category matching. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Register each view filter as a checkable command with a palette entry and profile keys, and wire the reserved Toggle Caulk Filter binding. Split hint from skip and add Quake II translucent and Quake III fog kinds. Let game or project data define kinds by texture pattern, surfaceparm, flag or class. Add the map filters CLI query that the module header already describes, and a smoke test for category matching.

reviews.workflow: There is no command that crashes the studio on purpose. With **Keep a crash report on this machine** on, a real crash writes a report and the next start offers it; kept reports are reviewed under **Help > Crash Reports…** (see Show Crash Report Dialog).
reviews.limitation: A developer-only fault trigger with no use in mapping. VibeStudio tests crash capture without crashing: studio_runtime_smoke_test checks report formatting and parsing, and checkCrashRecovery writes a dead-session marker and a report to drive the recovery offer. No in-app trigger exercises the signal handler on a real fault; tests use fixture reports instead. Crash capture on native macOS and Linux still needs acceptance.

reviews.workflow: **Wrap/Merge with Points** and `map wrap-merge --point` build a convex hull from selected objects plus up to three typed points; the clipper's wrap mode does the same with placed points. `map insert-vertices` and **Insert Vertex** in **Edit Brush Components…** add typed corners to an existing brush and rebuild its hull.
reviews.limitation: No route creates a brush directly from a typed point list. Wrap-merge needs source objects and accepts at most three extra points; vertex insertion needs an existing brush and --allow-collapse to drop its original corners. The core envelope builder used by wrap-merge is not exposed as its own command. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add **Create Brush from Points…** (palette and Create tools) and `map add-brush --points "x,y,z x,y,z …"` that build the convex envelope of four or more non-coplanar points with the current material as one undo step, using createLevelBrushEnvelope and addLevelMapBrushHulls.

reviews.workflow: **Add Brush…** previews a box (or another primitive) with typed **Centre** and **Size** for each axis and a chosen material. Set the centre to 0,0,0 and give all three sizes the same value to get the cube. `map add-brush --shape box --mins … --maxs … --texture …` and `map add-shape` do the same from the CLI.
reviews.limitation: The dialog starts at the view centre with a grid-based size rather than at the origin, and asks for three sizes rather than one; the CLI takes mins and maxs. Quake-family .map files only. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Edit Brush Components…** lists the selected brush's zero-based vertices with editable X, Y and Z coordinates, and edge and face centres in the other modes. `map brush-components --brush N` prints every solved vertex, edge and face (vertex IDs and material); --json gives full-precision coordinates.
reviews.limitation: One brush per dialog or command: there is no whole-selection dump, and the dialog needs exactly one selected brush. Faces list vertex IDs rather than coordinates. The dialog shows ten significant digits and plain-text CLI output six; use --json for exact values. There is no log-to-console action. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a **Copy Vertex Coordinates** command that writes every selected brush's or face's vertices at full precision to the clipboard or Log, and let `map brush-components` take repeated --brush selectors and print face vertex coordinates.

reviews.workflow: There is no command to type a window size. The studio restores its last window geometry at start, and UI tests set the shell size in code (for example 1440 × 900) when they take snapshots.
reviews.limitation: A debug-build helper for TrenchBroom developers taking fixed-size screenshots. Window size is the operating system's job and has no bearing on idTech1-3 mapping. You cannot type an exact window size; use the window manager. Restored geometry on native macOS and Linux still needs acceptance.

reviews.workflow: **Help > Crash Reports…** lists the reports kept on this machine, newest first, with a summary, the full text, **Copy Report** and **Show in Folder**. After a crash, the next start shows **View Report** and **Reopen Last Session**. `diagnostics crashes` lists the same reports with time, reason and report path.
reviews.limitation: There is no preview with a sample report: when none are kept, the command only says so in the status bar. There is no button that opens an issue tracker. Reports hold the session log tail, not a crash-time copy of the map; unsaved work relies on map recovery checkpoints. Crash capture on native macOS and Linux still needs acceptance.

reviews.workflow: There is no palette inspector. applyStudioTheme applies colours from StudioThemeTokens, Preferences chooses the theme (including both high-visibility themes), and studio_theme_smoke_test checks the tokens.
reviews.limitation: Developer theme inspection with no use in mapping. VibeStudio's colours come from its own theme tokens, which automated theme tests check; users choose themes in Preferences. There is no live view of the resolved Qt palette roles. Theme rendering on native macOS and Linux still needs acceptance.

reviews.workflow: There is no fault-injection command. Map edits go through core services designed to commit one undo step or leave the document unchanged; with locks present, guardLevelSceneEdit runs the edit on a candidate copy first. Smoke tests run refused edits directly.
reviews.limitation: Fault injection for TrenchBroom's command processor, which mappers never need. VibeStudio smoke tests cover refusal paths by feeding invalid input instead. No injected fault tests rollback after an unexpected exception part-way through an edit; refusal paths are tested only through invalid input.

reviews.workflow: **Hollow…** (Ctrl+Shift+K in the TrenchBroom profile) asks for a wall thickness, defaulting to the grid, and builds overlapping walls. **Hollow Touching…** builds walls that meet without overlapping, which is closest to TrenchBroom. `map hollow --mode overlap|touch|room` covers both headlessly, each as one undo step.
reviews.limitation: Both commands always prompt for a thickness. The TrenchBroom binding opens the overlapping variant, not touching walls. Wall decomposition can differ from TB's subtraction fragments. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **CSG Intersect** (Tools > Brush) replaces the selected brushes with their common volume, placed in the first brush's entity, and each face keeps its source texture. Brushes that do not overlap are refused and nothing changes. The edit is one undo step, and `map intersect` shares the core.
reviews.limitation: There is no Ctrl+L binding; the TrenchBroom profile already gives Ctrl+L to **Launch Game**. Refusing brushes that do not overlap may differ from how TB handles an empty result. `map intersect` has no dedicated CLI test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Carve** (Tools > Brush; Ctrl+K in the TrenchBroom profile) cuts the selected brushes out of every brush they overlap. Opened faces take the carving faces' textures, hidden brushes are left alone and scene locks block the edit. The whole carve is one undo step. `map carve` runs the same core.
reviews.limitation: The carving brushes stay selected, ready to delete, instead of being removed, and the fragments are not selected. Brushes written on shared source lines are skipped with a reason. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In a Quake III map, select world brushes, choose a patch shape such as **Patch Plane** in the Levels Shapes tab and press **Replace Selected Brushes**. One patch fills their combined bounds (a plane lies across the top) and is selected, as one undo step. `map add-shape --object` does the same headlessly. **Edit Vertices** then reshapes its control points.
reviews.limitation: Whole brushes are replaced by one patch; selected faces are not each turned into their own patch. Face materials and alignment are not carried over (the shape's texture is used), brush-entity brushes are refused and control-point editing is not entered automatically. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add a core conversion for Quake III maps that emits one planar patch per selected brush face (or per face of selected brushes), with configurable rows and columns and with material and UVs projected from the face mapping, as one undo step. Expose it as a GUI command with a palette entry, a TrenchBroom binding (Ctrl+P is the global **Go to File**, so scope it to the map context) and a map convert-patches CLI command, then enter Edit Vertices.

reviews.workflow: **Move Selection…** (Edit menu, Tools > Transform) takes x,y or x,y,z, defaulting to one grid step on X. It moves the whole selection through the shared placement service with Texture Lock, as one undo step. `map move` does the same job headlessly with --texture-lock.
reviews.limitation: There is no TrenchBroom-profile binding: TB's Ctrl+Alt+M is already used by **Copy Project Manifest**. The prompt defaults to one grid step, not 0 0 0. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Find and Replace Textures…** (Edit, Tools > Surfaces, the object menu and command search) takes the texture to replace, chosen from the map's textures, typed, or picked on the Textures tab, and its replacement. **Picked faces** replaces only the picked faces, matching TrenchBroom's selected-face case; **Whole map** and **Selected objects** cover the rest. A live count updates as you type. The Textures tab and package browser open it with the replacement already chosen. It covers brushes, patches and Doom sides and sectors as one undo step; hidden, filtered and locked uses are skipped and counted. `map replace-texture` (with `--face`) shares the core.
reviews.limitation: The fields list only textures already in the map plus free text; browsing every package material happens on the Textures tab or surface, whose picks fill the fields. TrenchBroom's success and failure message boxes are status-bar messages instead. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Snap Vertices to Grid** (Tools > Vertices) rounds the vertices of the selected brushes, and of the brushes of selected entities, onto the current grid and rebuilds them. Brushes that would collapse are left as they were, with a reason, and the edit is one undo step. `map snap-vertices --grid N` shares the core. The TrenchBroom profile binds Ctrl+Alt+Shift+V.
reviews.limitation: Whether brushes reached only through a nested group selection are included is unverified, and `map snap-vertices` has no dedicated CLI test. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: Choose **Grid 1**, then run **Snap Vertices to Grid** (Tools > Vertices) on the selected brushes and the brushes of selected entities. Brushes that would collapse are skipped with a reason, and the edit is one undo step. `map snap-vertices --grid 1` does the job in one CLI call.
reviews.limitation: There is no one-step GUI command and no Ctrl+Shift+V binding, so the grid has to be changed and then restored. Whether brushes reached only through a nested group selection are included is unverified. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Texture Lock** (Edit menu, the Levels **Transform** tool group and the palette) is a saved checkable setting. Moves, quick turns, flips, shears, numeric rotation, paste, prefabs and face extrusion use it, and **Texture Scale Lock** governs resizing. CLI transforms take `--texture-lock on|off`.
reviews.limitation: An exact lock on classic faces can need explicit Valve 220 conversion through **Allow Valve 220 Conversion**. Resizing follows a separate scale lock instead of one shared toggle. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: In the TrenchBroom profile, dragging over empty space in a 2D view draws a box or the chosen shape. **Draw Brush in Camera** drags a footprint in the 3D view, with the wheel setting depth. **Add Brush…** previews primitives first. **Wrap/Merge with Points** hulls selected objects with up to three typed points. `map add-brush`, `map add-shape` and `map wrap-merge` script these.
reviews.limitation: There is no point-by-point convex assembly from clicked points, no face-extrusion polygon workflow and no B binding; Wrap/Merge needs source objects and takes at most three typed points. The production plan records arbitrary convex creation as open. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Build a checkable assemble tool. It collects grid- or surface-snapped points in plan and camera views, previews their convex hull using the Wrap/Merge hull code, allows face drag-extrusion and commits on Enter as one undo step. Bind B in the TrenchBroom profile and add a palette entry.

reviews.workflow: **Edit Vertices** (Tools > Vertices) shows patch control points beside brush vertices in plan and camera views. Points can be picked, dragged, nudged and transformed with the component tools, each edit one undo step. **Edit Patch Control Points…** sets exact positions, UVs and subdivision. `map edit-patch` and `map transform-components` script these edits.
reviews.limitation: Patch points share the vertex mode instead of having a dedicated tool, there is no P binding, and patch points are not quick-snap targets. The production plan still lists wider patch transform and UV workflows as open. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Rotate Selection…** (Tools > Transform) previews any angle about the selection centre, the world origin or a custom pivot, with Texture Lock. **Rotate 90° Left/Right** turn by quarter turns as the active view shows the map. **Rotate Components** drags rings for picked components only. `map rotate` scripts rotation.
reviews.limitation: There is no rotation handle for whole objects, no draggable centre in the views and no R binding. The ring gizmo works only on vertex, edge and face picks. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Extend the component ring gizmo to whole selections (brushes, patches and entities with angle keys), with a movable pivot, angle-step snapping and Texture Lock, and one undo step per drag. Add a checkable tool, a palette entry and the TrenchBroom R binding.

reviews.workflow: When something is selected, 2D views show edge and corner resize handles and the camera shows labelled X, Y and Z face handles. **Resize Selection…** (Tools > Transform) takes exact sizes and the point that stays fixed. **Texture Scale Lock** decides whether textures stretch. `map resize` scripts resizing.
reviews.limitation: The handles are always shown rather than toggled with T. There are no proportional or centre-scaling modifiers, and the camera has no edge or corner handles. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add proportional (Shift) and about-centre (Alt) modifiers to plan and camera resize drags, add edge and corner handles in the camera, and give the TrenchBroom profile a tool toggle bound to T.

reviews.workflow: **Shear Tool** (Tools > Transform) shows side handles in 2D views. Dragging one slants the selection about the opposite side, following Texture Lock, and Escape turns the tool off. **Shear…** slants by a typed angle about the centre, **Shear Components** works on picks, and `map shear` scripts shearing.
reviews.limitation: There are no shear handles in the 3D camera and no G binding in the TrenchBroom profile. Where the face format cannot slant textures, the tool shears without texture lock. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open. Remaining work: Add camera shear handles on the faces of the selection's box, reusing the camera resize handles, with a modifier for vertical shear. Add a palette entry and the TrenchBroom G binding.

reviews.workflow: **Lock Component UVs** is a saved toggle, separate from Texture Lock, in Geometry, Tools > Vertices and the palette; the TrenchBroom profile binds it to U, which is not one of that profile's camera fly keys (W, S, A, D, Q, X). It keeps corner texture coordinates during component drags, numeric transforms and rounding. With **Fit UVs When Lock Fails** (on by default) a deformation one planar projection cannot follow is no longer refused: the face is fitted to three corners and the status bar counts fitted faces. Patch control points keep their UVs. CLI: `map transform-components --uv-lock off|on|fit`.
reviews.limitation: TrenchBroom re-fits each face from its matching old face; VibeStudio keeps exact corner UVs where it can and otherwise fits three corners, unmoved corners first, so drifting corners can differ from TrenchBroom. Insertion, splitting, removal and face extrusion follow their own mapping policies. Native physical input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Help > About VibeStudio** (Shift+F1) shows the version, platform, imported compilers and credits. `about show` prints the same information.
reviews.limitation: The About dialog itself has no UI test; only its registration and the CLI output are tested. On macOS, its placement in the native application menu has not been checked. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **File > Close Map** asks about unsaved edits (**Save**, **Discard Edits**, **Cancel**) and retires recovery. It then clears the views and the leak trail, and the studio stays open.
reviews.limitation: Close Map has no default shortcut; Ctrl+W is **Close Package**. Loaded portal outlines stay after the map closes. Native physical-input and macOS/Linux acceptance remain open.

reviews.workflow: **Save Map As…** writes the whole map to another path. `map copy` writes chosen objects to a separate fragment .map and leaves the source alone. **Save Region As…** writes a sealed region as a map of its own without changing the open document's path.
reviews.limitation: Unlike TrenchBroom's export, Save Map As makes the new path the document's own. Save Region As only covers a region and adds seal brushes. Scene layers have no Omit From Export flag, so there is no way to write the map without chosen layers. Remaining work: Add Export Map…, which writes a copy through writeLevelDocument without taking over the path and refuses the current file. It should leave out layers flagged Omit From Export, with the flag stored in the scene metadata. Add a matching `map export` CLI command with an omit-layer option and a dry run.

reviews.workflow: VibeStudio cannot export a map as OBJ. **Export Map Image…** writes an SVG picture of the map, and the Models surface exports single model frames as OBJ. Existing control: None
reviews.limitation: Brushes and patches cannot be taken into Blender or another modeller. The existing OBJ writer only handles model frames. Remaining work: Write OBJ and MTL from the camera mesh: brush faces and tessellated patches with UVs, grouped by material. Write material paths relative to the game or the export folder, and skip hidden objects. Add File > Export Map as OBJ… and a `map export-obj` CLI command with a dry run.
